# anyhow - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/anyhow/^1.0.93/

## Expand description

This library provides [ anyhow::Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html), a trait object based error
type for easy idiomatic error handling in Rust applications.

[§](https://docs.rs#details)Details

-
Use `Result<T, anyhow::Error>`, or equivalently`anyhow::Result<T>`, as the return type of any fallible function.Within the function, use `?`to easily propagate any error that implements the`std::error::Error``use anyhow::Result; fn get_cluster_info() -> Result<ClusterMap> { let config = std::fs::read_to_string("cluster.json")?; let map: ClusterMap = serde_json::from_str(&config)?; Ok(map) }`
-
Attach context to help the person troubleshooting the error understand where things went wrong. A low-level error like “No such file or directory” can be annoying to debug without more context about what higher level step the application was in the middle of. `use anyhow::{Context, Result}; fn main() -> Result<()> { ... it.detach().context("Failed to detach the important thing")?; let content = std::fs::read(path) .with_context(|| format!("Failed to read instrs from {}", path))?; ... }``Error: Failed to read instrs from ./path/to/instrs.json Caused by: No such file or directory (os error 2)`
-
Downcasting is supported and can be by value, by shared reference, or by mutable reference as needed. `// If the error was caused by redaction, then return a // tombstone instead of the content. match root_cause.downcast_ref::<DataStoreError>() { Some(DataStoreError::Censored(_)) => Ok(Poll::Ready(REDACTED_CONTENT)), None => Err(error), }`
-
If using Rust ≥ 1.65, a backtrace is captured and printed with the error if the underlying error type does not already provide its own. In order to see backtraces, they must be enabled through the environment variables described in `std::backtrace`- If you want panics and errors to both have backtraces, set
`RUST_BACKTRACE=1`;
- If you want only errors to have backtraces, set `RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE=1`;
- If you want only panics to have backtraces, set `RUST_BACKTRACE=1`and`RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE=0`.

- If you want panics and errors to both have backtraces, set
-
Anyhow works with any error type that has an impl of `std::error::Error`, including ones defined in your crate. We do not bundle a`derive(Error)`macro but you can write the impls yourself or use a standalone macro like[thiserror](https://github.com/dtolnay/thiserror).`use thiserror::Error; #[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum FormatError { #[error("Invalid header (expected {expected:?}, got {found:?})")] InvalidHeader { expected: String, found: String, }, #[error("Missing attribute: {0}")] MissingAttribute(String), }`
-
One-off error messages can be constructed using the `anyhow!`macro, which supports string interpolation and produces an`anyhow::Error`.`return Err(anyhow!("Missing attribute: {}", missing));`A `bail!`macro is provided as a shorthand for the same early return.`bail!("Missing attribute: {}", missing);`

[§](https://docs.rs#no-std-support)No-std support

In no_std mode, almost all of the same API is available and works the same way. To depend on Anyhow in no_std mode, disable our default enabled “std” feature in Cargo.toml. A global allocator is required.

```
[dependencies]
anyhow = { version = "1.0", default-features = false }
```
With versions of Rust older than 1.81, no_std mode may require an additional
`.map_err(Error::msg)` when working with a non-Anyhow error type inside a
function that returns Anyhow’s error type, as the trait that `?`-based error
conversions are defined by is only available in std in those old versions.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [anyhow](https://docs.rs/macro.anyhow.html)as format_err;

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [anyhow](https://docs.rs/macro.anyhow.html)
- Construct an ad-hoc error from a string or existing non-`anyhow`error value.
- [bail](https://docs.rs/macro.bail.html)
- Return early with an error.
- [ensure](https://docs.rs/macro.ensure.html)
- Return early with an error if a condition is not satisfied.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Chain](https://docs.rs/struct.Chain.html)
- Iterator of a chain of source errors.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)
- The `Error`type, a wrapper around a dynamic error type.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Context](https://docs.rs/trait.Context.html)
- Provides the `context`method for`Result`.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [Ok](https://docs.rs/fn.Ok.html)
- Equivalent to `Ok::<_, anyhow::Error>(value)`.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Result](https://docs.rs/type.Result.html)

# heck - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/heck/^0.5/

## Expand description

**heck** is a case conversion library.

This library exists to provide case conversion between common cases like CamelCase and snake_case. It is intended to be unicode aware, internally consistent, and reasonably well performing.

[§](https://docs.rs#definition-of-a-word-boundary)Definition of a word boundary

Word boundaries are defined by non-alphanumeric characters, as well as within those words in this manner:

- If an uppercase character is followed by lowercase letters, a word boundary is considered to be just prior to that uppercase character.
- If multiple uppercase characters are consecutive, they are considered to be within a single word, except that the last will be part of the next word if it is followed by lowercase characters (see rule 1).

That is, “HelloWorld” is segmented `Hello|World` whereas “XMLHttpRequest” is
segmented `XML|Http|Request`.

Characters not within words (such as spaces, punctuations, and underscores) are not included in the output string except as they are a part of the case being converted to. Multiple adjacent word boundaries (such as a series of underscores) are folded into one. (“hello__world” in snake case is therefore “hello_world”, not the exact same string). Leading or trailing word boundary indicators are dropped, except insofar as CamelCase capitalizes the first word.

[§](https://docs.rs#cases-contained-in-this-library)Cases contained in this library:

- UpperCamelCase
- lowerCamelCase
- snake_case
- kebab-case
- SHOUTY_SNAKE_CASE
- Title Case
- SHOUTY-KEBAB-CASE
- Train-Case

# indexmap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/indexmap/^2.0.0/

## Expand description

[ IndexMap](https://docs.rs/map/struct.IndexMap.html) is a hash table where the iteration order of the key-value
pairs is independent of the hash values of the keys.

[ IndexSet](https://docs.rs/set/struct.IndexSet.html) is a corresponding hash set using the same implementation and
with similar properties.

[§](https://docs.rs#highlights)Highlights

[ IndexMap](https://docs.rs/map/struct.IndexMap.html) and

[are drop-in compatible with the std](https://docs.rs/set/struct.IndexSet.html)

`IndexSet``HashMap`
and `HashSet`, but they also have some features of note:- The ordering semantics (see their documentation for details)
- Sorting methods and the `.pop()`
- The `Equivalent`
- The `MutableKeys``MutableValues`

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature Flags

To reduce the amount of compiled code in the crate by default, certain
features are gated behind [feature flags](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html#the-features-section). These allow you to opt in to (or
out of) functionality. Below is a list of the features available in this
crate.

- `std`: Enables features which require the Rust standard library. For more information see the section on- `no_std`
- `rayon`: Enables parallel iteration and other parallel methods.
- `serde`: Adds implementations for- `Serialize`- `Deserialize`- `IndexMap`- `IndexSet`- `IndexMap`- `map::serde_seq`
- `arbitrary`: Adds implementations for the- `arbitrary::Arbitrary`- `IndexMap`- `IndexSet`
- `quickcheck`: Adds implementations for the- `quickcheck::Arbitrary`- `IndexMap`- `IndexSet`
- `borsh`(- **deprecated**): Adds implementations for- `BorshSerialize`- `BorshDeserialize`- `IndexMap`- `IndexSet`- `borsh`- `indexmap`,- `borsh v1.5.6`added an- `indexmap`feature that should be used instead of enabling the feature here.

*Note: only the  std feature is enabled by default.*

[§](https://docs.rs#alternate-hashers)Alternate Hashers

[ IndexMap](https://docs.rs/map/struct.IndexMap.html) and

[have a default hasher type](https://docs.rs/set/struct.IndexSet.html)

`IndexSet`[, just like the standard](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/hash/random/struct.RandomState.html)

`S = RandomState``HashMap` and `HashSet`, which is resistant to
HashDoS attacks but not the most performant. Type aliases can make it easier
to use alternate hashers:```
use fnv::FnvBuildHasher;
use indexmap::{IndexMap, IndexSet};
type FnvIndexMap<K, V> = IndexMap<K, V, FnvBuildHasher>;
type FnvIndexSet<T> = IndexSet<T, FnvBuildHasher>;
let std: IndexSet<i32> = (0..100).collect();
let fnv: FnvIndexSet<i32> = (0..100).collect();
assert_eq!(std, fnv);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#rust-version)Rust Version

This version of indexmap requires Rust 1.85 or later.

The indexmap 2.x release series will use a carefully considered version upgrade policy, where in a later 2.x version, we will raise the minimum required Rust version.

[§](https://docs.rs#no-standard-library-targets)No Standard Library Targets

This crate supports being built without `std`, requiring `alloc` instead.
This is chosen by disabling the default “std” cargo feature, by adding
`default-features = false` to your dependency specification.

- Creating maps and sets using `new``with_capacity``std`. Use methods`IndexMap::default``with_hasher``with_capacity_and_hasher``twox-hash`.
- Macros `indexmap!``indexset!``std`. Use the macros`indexmap_with_default!``indexset_with_default!`

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (c397dae80 2026-07-02)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

---

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

---

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# bamboo_infrastructure - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bamboo-infrastructure/2026.7.3/bamboo_infrastructure/

## Expand description

Bamboo infrastructure — process management, logging, and metrics.

This crate provides infrastructure-level utilities that are tightly coupled to the process environment (shell discovery, command building, window hiding).

Higher-level crates (LLM, config, storage, A2A) each have their own dedicated
crate (`bamboo-llm`, `bamboo-config`, `bamboo-storage`, `bamboo-a2a`) and should
be imported directly rather than through this crate.

Token budget management for LLM conversations.

# ddd_cqrs_es - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ddd_cqrs_es/0.2.5/ddd_cqrs_es/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#ddd_cqrs_es)ddd_cqrs_es

A lightweight framework for building Domain-Driven Design, CQRS, and Event Sourcing applications in Rust.

The crate provides explicit building blocks for aggregate command handling, optimistic concurrency, event replay, projections, process managers, snapshots, and pluggable persistence backends. The included in-memory store is intended for tests, examples, and local development.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use ddd_cqrs_es::{Aggregate, DomainEvent, InMemoryEventStore, Metadata, Repository};
#[derive(Clone)]
enum CounterEvent {
    Created,
    Incremented(u64),
}
impl DomainEvent for CounterEvent {
    fn event_type(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            CounterEvent::Created => "counter_created",
            CounterEvent::Incremented(_) => "counter_incremented",
        }
    }
}
enum CounterCommand {
    Create,
    Increment(u64),
}
#[derive(Default)]
struct Counter {
    exists: bool,
    value: u64,
    revision: u64,
}
#[derive(Debug)]
enum CounterError {
    AlreadyCreated,
    NotCreated,
}
impl Aggregate for Counter {
    type Id = String;
    type Command = CounterCommand;
    type Event = CounterEvent;
    type Error = CounterError;
    fn aggregate_type() -> &'static str { "counter" }
    fn revision(&self) -> u64 { self.revision }
    fn new() -> Self { Self::default() }
    fn apply(&mut self, event: &Self::Event) {
        match event {
            CounterEvent::Created => self.exists = true,
            CounterEvent::Incremented(by) => self.value += by,
        }
        self.revision += 1;
    }
    fn handle(&self, command: Self::Command) -> Result<Vec<Self::Event>, Self::Error> {
        match command {
            CounterCommand::Create if self.exists => Err(CounterError::AlreadyCreated),
            CounterCommand::Create => Ok(vec![CounterEvent::Created]),
            CounterCommand::Increment(_) if !self.exists => Err(CounterError::NotCreated),
            CounterCommand::Increment(by) => Ok(vec![CounterEvent::Incremented(by)]),
        }
    }
}
let store = InMemoryEventStore::<Counter>::new();
let repo = Repository::new(store);
let counter_id = "counter-1".to_owned();
repo.execute(&counter_id, CounterCommand::Create, Metadata::default())?;
repo.execute(&counter_id, CounterCommand::Increment(5), Metadata::default())?;
let loaded = repo.load(&counter_id)?;
assert_eq!(loaded.state.value, 5);
```

# gpur 0.8.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gpur/0.8.1

# gpur

btop-style GPU monitor for the terminal. An `nvtop` replacement that runs
everywhere: NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, and Apple GPUs on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

Mirrored braille waveforms, gradient meters, an nvtop-style process table with per-process GPU attribution, mouse support, foldable GPU cards, and theming via the hjkl stack.

Status: beta.The AMD Linux path is battle-tested on real hardware, and the macOS IOKit backend returns live data (validated against macOS CI runners' paravirt GPU — Apple Silicon numbers still welcome). Intel and Windows backends are implemented, CI-exercised, and awaiting real-GPU reports.

## Install

Debian/RPM packages, musl builds, and an Alpine `.apk` are attached to each
[GitHub release](https://github.com/kryptic-sh/gpur/releases).

## Run

## Keys & mouse

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| `q`/`Esc` | quit |
| `Space` | pause/resume polling |
| `0`-`9` | focus GPU list + select GPU N; same digit again folds it |
| `p` | focus process list |
| `j`/`k`, arrows | move within the focused pane |
| `J`/`K`, PgUp/PgDn | move the process cursor from anywhere |
| `s`/`r` | cycle process sort column / reverse it |
| `/` | filter processes (Enter applies, empty clears) |
| `x`/`X` | SIGTERM / SIGKILL the selected process (with confirm) |
| `+`/`=`/`-` | poll rate faster/slower |
| wheel / click | scroll + focus the pane under the cursor; click selects |

## Configuration

`gpur` reads `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/gpur/config.toml` (falls back to
`~/.config/gpur/config.toml`). No file is written automatically; missing file
means built-in defaults.

```
 = 1000
 = 300
# graph glyphs: "braille" (default), "block", or "ascii" for fonts
# without braille coverage
 = "braille"
# hjkl-theme TOML; omit for the built-in theme
 = "/path/to/theme.toml"
```
Themes use the [hjkl-theme](https://crates.io/crates/hjkl-theme) schema:
`[palette]` of hex colors plus `[ui]` styles. Any hjkl theme file works — the
meters, waveform gradients, and highlights all derive from the palette.

## Backends

| Backend | Platform | Source | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| nvml | Linux, Windows | NVML (dynamic load) | done |
| amdgpu | Linux | sysfs `/sys/class/drm`+ fdinfo | done |
| intel | Linux | i915/xe fdinfo + hwmon | done |
| pdh | Windows | GPU Engine/Adapter Memory + DXGI | done |
| ioaccel | macOS | IOAccelerator PerfStats (IOKit) | done |
| mock | all | deterministic waves ( `--mock`) | done |

Probe order: nvml → amdgpu → intel → ioaccel → pdh. Intel utilization is derived from per-client fdinfo engine counters (i915 busy-ns, xe cycles) the same way nvtop does it; power comes from the hwmon energy counter delta. PDH is the vendor-generic Windows fallback (Task Manager's counters) and reports utilization and memory only.

Backend poll failures degrade gracefully: the last snapshot stays on screen with a header warning until polling recovers — a driver reset won't kill the monitor.

Extras: each GPU card shows session peaks/averages (util, temp, power) when tall
enough, and the PCIe caption flags a link running below its maximum
(`PCIe 3.0@8x (max 4.0@16x)`) — a classic symptom of a bad riser or wrong slot.

Encoder/decoder activity shows in each card (split `enc`/`dec` on
NVIDIA/Windows, unified `video` on AMD/Intel), and a red throttle badge appears
when the GPU is thermal- or power-limited (real reasons on NVIDIA, at-limit
heuristic on AMD).

Planned depth: Apple temperature/power (SMC/IOReport), Windows AMD ADLX (temps/fans/clocks).

## Per-process GPU attribution

The process table (PID, user, device, type, GPU%, GPU memory, CPU%, host memory,
command) works on Linux (AMD + Intel via `/proc` fdinfo — same-user processes
unless run as root), NVIDIA everywhere (NVML), and Windows (PDH per-pid
counters). macOS has no public per-process GPU API. On Linux, containerized
processes get a CONTAINER column (docker/podman/k8s id from cgroups).

Recorded sessions replay: `gpur --log run.jsonl` while it happens, then
`gpur --replay run.jsonl` anywhere — including machines with no GPU — with the
recorded process attribution intact. Ideal for bug reports.

## License

MIT

# bamboo_broker - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bamboo-broker/2026.7.3/bamboo_broker/

## Expand description

`bamboo-broker` — a standalone network message broker for sub-agent
ask/reply (and future task/handoff) traffic.

The broker fronts durable per-session [ Mailbox](https://docs.rs/bamboo-subagent/2026.7.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bamboo_subagent/mailbox/struct.Mailbox.html)
queues with a WebSocket bus, so a central orchestrator and its workers —
local subprocesses, local Docker containers, or SSH/remote hosts — exchange
messages over the network with durability and at-least-once delivery, without
sharing a filesystem.

Topology: a single central broker (hub-and-spoke). It is a *pure message
bus* — it routes messages, it does not spawn actors or coordinate with other
brokers. Spawning the PUSH-side workers lives in [ deploy](https://docs.rs/deploy/index.html) (the

`Deployer`
family: local / docker / ssh / russh). (The `bamboo_subagent::WorkerLauncher`
trait that earlier docs referenced was never wired and has been removed; the
PULL-side actor runner dispatches placement inline.)Layers:

- `proto`
- `core`- `BrokerCore`
- the WebSocket server + auth + `bamboo broker serve`wiring layer on top (added next).

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use crate::ask::`- [ask_agent](https://docs.rs/ask/fn.ask_agent.html);
- `pub use crate::ask::`- [ask_over](https://docs.rs/ask/fn.ask_over.html);
- `pub use crate::ask::`- [request_over](https://docs.rs/ask/fn.request_over.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [ask](https://docs.rs/ask/index.html)
- Orchestrator-side ask: deliver an `Ask`to a target agent over the broker and await its correlated`Reply`. This is the primitive the`SubAgent`“ask” action (and tests) build on —`me`asks`target`a question and judges the answer, regardless of where`target`physically runs.
- [child_](https://docs.rs/child_link/index.html)- link
- `BrokerChildLink`— the parent side of running a child over the mailbox bus.
- [client](https://docs.rs/client/index.html)
- Broker client. Connects, does the `Hello`handshake, then runs a background reader that demuxes incoming frames into a`messages`stream and a`delivered`receipt stream — so one connection can both deliver and subscribe (the parent does both: deliver an Ask, subscribe for the Reply).
- [core](https://docs.rs/core/index.html)
- Broker routing core: per-session durable mailboxes + push subscriptions.
- [deploy](https://docs.rs/deploy/index.html)
- Deployers: bring up a `bamboo broker-agent serve`somewhere — as a local subprocess, in a Docker container, or on a remote host over SSH — pointed at a central broker. This is the orchestrator-side “push” model (the master deploys execution environments; workers dial home to the broker), as opposed to mutual discovery.
- [deploy_](https://docs.rs/deploy_russh/index.html)- russh
- `RusshDeployer`— deploy a- `broker-agent`worker over an in-process SSH connection (- `russh`- `ssh`cannot accept cleanly.
- [mcp](https://docs.rs/mcp/index.html)
- MCP-over-broker proxy (P2): a remote/deployed worker invokes host-bound MCP servers (e.g. nova — needs the screen/local creds) that physically run on the orchestrator, by forwarding the tool calls over the broker.
- [mux](https://docs.rs/mux/index.html)
- Request/reply MULTIPLEXER over a single broker connection.
- [proto](https://docs.rs/proto/index.html)
- Broker wire protocol: client ↔ broker frames, JSON over WebSocket text.
- [serve](https://docs.rs/serve/index.html)
- Mailbox serving loop: the worker side of the bus.
- [server](https://docs.rs/server/index.html)
- WebSocket server: a thin network shell over `BrokerCore`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Agent](https://docs.rs/struct.AgentRef.html)- Ref
- Sender identity attached to an inbox message.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Broker](https://docs.rs/enum.BrokerError.html)- Error
- Errors from broker operations.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [ORCHESTRATOR_](https://docs.rs/constant.ORCHESTRATOR_ID.html)- ID
- The orchestrator’s broker mailbox id — where workers send MCP proxy requests
and where `serve_mcp_proxy`listens. A fixed well-known id (single MCP host).

# ikigai_personal - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ikigai-personal/0.3.1/ikigai_personal/

## Expand description

`ikigai-personal` — personal contexts for ikigai.

Late-bound, OS-backed resources under `urn:personal:*` — your contacts,
calendar, and free/busy availability — resolved through the local operating
system rather than a remote service, so the data never leaves the machine.

[§](https://docs.rs#platform-support)Platform support

macOS is the first backend. **Windows and Linux are placeholders today**: the
crate *builds* on them, but the personal resources resolve to a clear
“not supported yet” error until their backends land (Windows: Microsoft Graph
/ Active Directory; Linux: LDAP / CalDAV / D-Bus). The macOS backend currently
returns clearly-labelled **sample data** pending the real Contacts/EventKit
integration.

[§](https://docs.rs#capability-scoping)Capability scoping

Access is gated by `urn:cap:` capability scopes (see `ikigai-core`’s
`Capability`). `urn:personal:calendar` projects on the capability: a holder of
`urn:cap:personal:calendar:read:detail` sees full detail; one with only
`…:read:freebusy` sees busy blocks (no titles or attendees); one with neither
is denied. That’s the data-minimization story — *“an agent books around my
week without ever learning what I’m doing”* — and it’s why detail and free/busy
are one resource with two capability-scoped views rather than two resources.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Calendar](https://docs.rs/struct.CalendarConfig.html)- Config
- Configuration for the consolidated-view calendar machinery — the
hand-editable file a host loads (conventionally
`~/.config/ikigai/calendar.json`).
- [Calendar](https://docs.rs/struct.CalendarInfo.html)- Info
- One native calendar, as the OS reports it.
- [Event](https://docs.rs/struct.EventInfo.html)- Info
- One calendar event, normalized from the OS store.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [availability](https://docs.rs/fn.availability.html)
- `availability`: the free/busy projection for a period — busy blocks only, gated on- `urn:cap:personal:calendar:read:freebusy`.
- [calendar](https://docs.rs/fn.calendar.html)
- `calendar`: real events for a period, projected on the capability — full detail with- `…:read:detail`(and a Turtle face via- `as=text/turtle`), free/busy with- `…:read:freebusy`, denied with neither.
- [calendar_](https://docs.rs/fn.calendar_config.html)- config
- `calendar:config`: the effective consolidated-view configuration the host loaded (view name, source allowlist, inbox, account) — or a pointer to create the file if none was found.
- [calendars](https://docs.rs/fn.calendars.html)
- `calendars`: the native calendar collection.- `Source`lists every calendar with its account;- `Sink`creates one —- `name=`(default: the configured view) on- `account=`(default: configured account, else iCloud, else the system default). Real EventKit; the first use may raise the macOS calendar-access prompt.
- [contacts](https://docs.rs/fn.contacts.html)
- `contacts`: the local address book, gated on- `urn:cap:personal:contacts:read`.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_supported.html)- supported
- Whether a personal backend is implemented for the platform this was built for.
- [platform_](https://docs.rs/fn.platform_name.html)- name
- The human-readable name of the platform this was built for.
- [space](https://docs.rs/fn.space.html)
- The personal-contexts space: binds the resources at `urn:personal:*`. The optional`CalendarConfig``~/.config/ikigai/calendar.json`) parameterizes the consolidated-view machinery;`None`leaves the read resources fully functional.

# bamboo_subagent - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bamboo-subagent/2026.7.3/bamboo_subagent/

## Expand description

`bamboo-subagent` — sub-agent fleet runtime.

Slice 1 (this build): pure filesystem logic, no runtime dependency.

- `store`
- `mailbox`

See `docs/subagent-actor-runtime-design.md` (§3.4, §5) and
`docs/subagent-store-mailbox-interface.md` for the design these implement.

The session payload is kept opaque (generic `T: Serialize`/`DeserializeOwned`) so this
crate stays a leaf and is fully unit-testable with a tempdir; higher layers pass the
domain `Session`. Index rebuild is decoupled via the [ store::MetaExtractor](https://docs.rs/store/trait.MetaExtractor.html) seam.

# ikigai_rdf - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ikigai-rdf/0.1.3/ikigai_rdf/

## Expand description

`ikigai-rdf` — RDF **transreption** as an ikigai resource.

`urn:rdf:transrept` takes an RDF document and re-serializes it into another syntax,
chosen by the `as` argument (content negotiation): Turtle, N-Triples, N-Quads, TriG,
RDF/XML, JSON-LD, or a human-readable HTML table. The input syntax is sniffed (an
explicit format isn’t needed for the common cases).

It’s the first step toward NetKernel-style *transreption* — lossless transformation
between representations of the same resource. Built on Oxigraph’s **pure** parser/
serializer crates (`oxrdfio`/`oxrdf`) — no store, no rocksdb — so it compiles to
`wasm32` and the browser can transrept a fetched graph **client-side**:

`source urn:httpGet url=https://example.org/thing | urn:rdf:transrept as=text/turtle`The kernel pipes the fetched bytes into `content`; `as` picks the representation.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [space](https://docs.rs/fn.space.html)
- [subclass_](https://docs.rs/fn.subclass_axioms.html)- axioms
- Parse a Turtle alignment graph and return every `rdfs:subClassOf`axiom as a`(subclass, superclass)`IRI pair — the closure pairs a host feeds to the kernel’s type-aware action selection (`Kernel::with_subclass_axioms`), so an entity typed`foaf:Person`satisfies a`schema:Person`action. Best-effort: triples whose subject or object isn’t an IRI (blank nodes, literals) and any unparseable triples are skipped —`subClassOf`relates named classes.

# ikigai_org - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ikigai-org/0.1.0/ikigai_org/

## Expand description

`ikigai-org` — the org-mode agenda as ROC resources.

`urn:org:agenda:{period}` reads **date-fixed events** (headlines with active
`<…>` timestamps, repeaters expanded into the window) from org files and
serves them as text or as the **same skolemized Turtle event graph**
`urn:personal:calendar` speaks — so org and native calendars union and diff
as graphs (the Brian-Busy materialized-view plan).

The org files are read **through the kernel**: the host binds them (e.g. an
`ikigai-fs` space jailed to the org directory at `urn:orgfile:{path}`) and
hands this space their IRIs. That keeps this crate free of filesystem
access — capability-gated, wasm-clean, and golden-thread-ready when the
host’s file space is cacheable.

[§](https://docs.rs#what-is-parsed-v1)What is parsed (v1)

Headlines (`* Title`) whose section carries an active timestamp:
`<YYYY-MM-DD [Day] [HH:MM[-HH:MM]] [+N{d,w,m,y}]>`. Inactive `[…]`
timestamps are ignored. Untimed stamps are all-day; a timed stamp without
an end defaults to one hour. Repeaters (`+1w`, `+1y`, …) are expanded into
the requested window.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Agenda](https://docs.rs/struct.AgendaEndpoint.html)- Endpoint
- `urn:org:agenda[:{period}]`— the org agenda for a period (default- `week`), sourced through the kernel from the configured org-file resources.
- [OrgEvent](https://docs.rs/struct.OrgEvent.html)
- One agenda event, normalized. The same shape the calendar side speaks.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [agenda_](https://docs.rs/fn.agenda_events.html)- events
- Parse org text into the events overlapping `[win_start, win_end)`, expanding repeaters into the window.
- [space](https://docs.rs/fn.space.html)
- Mount the agenda: `urn:org:agenda`and`urn:org:agenda:{period}`, reading the given org-file resources through the kernel.

# pdfmuse_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pdfmuse-core/0.1.6/pdfmuse_core/

## Expand description

pdfmuse-core — deterministic PDF/DOCX parser core.

The naive `parse()` lands in PER-33 and the self-written content-stream
interpreter (the real value) in PER-36. The unified IR — the data foundation
that every binding serializes byte-identically — lives in [ ir](https://docs.rs/ir/index.html).

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use error::`- [PdfmuseError](https://docs.rs/error/enum.PdfmuseError.html);
- `pub use error::`- [Result](https://docs.rs/error/type.Result.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [backend](https://docs.rs/backend/index.html)
- Pluggable vision backend — the ML boundary.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- Structured error type.
- [ir](https://docs.rs/ir/index.html)
- Unified intermediate representation (IR).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Chunk](https://docs.rs/struct.Chunk.html)
- A retrieval unit: a block’s text plus the context needed to cite it.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [chunk](https://docs.rs/fn.chunk.html)
- Split `doc`into chunks (one per non-empty block), tracking heading context.
- [parse](https://docs.rs/fn.parse.html)
- Parse `data`into the unified`ir::Document`
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_with_password.html)- with_ - password
- Like `parse``password`for encrypted PDFs.
- [to_json](https://docs.rs/fn.to_json.html)
- Serialize the entire `Document`
- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_markdown.html)- markdown
- Render `doc`to GitHub-flavored Markdown, pages and blocks in order.
- [to_text](https://docs.rs/fn.to_text.html)
- Render `doc`to plain reading-order text — no Markdown syntax, just the block text joined by newlines. The cheapest useful output for search / ATS / feeding an LLM, and (via the bindings) avoids materializing the full IR on the host.

[251](#251)impl TrappableImports {
[252](#252)    fn can_trap(&self, f: &Function) -> bool {
[253](#253)        match self {
[254](#254)            TrappableImports::None => false,
[255](#255)            TrappableImports::All => true,
[256](#256)            TrappableImports::Only(set) => set.contains(&f.name),
[257](#257)        }
[258](#258)    }

[261](#261)impl Opts {
[262](#262)    pub fn generate(&self, resolve: &Resolve, world: WorldId) -> anyhow::Result<String> {
[263](#263)        if !cfg!(feature = "component-model-async")
[266](#266)            && resolve
[267](#267)                .types
[268](#268)                .iter()
[269](#269)                .any(|(_, ty)| matches!(ty.kind, TypeDefKind::Future(_) | TypeDefKind::Stream(_)))
[270](#270)        {
[271](#271)            anyhow::bail!(
[272](#272)                "must enable `component-model-async` feature when using WIT files \
[273](#273)                 containing future, stream, or error-context types"
[274](#274)            );
[275](#275)        }
[276](#276)
[277](#277)        let mut r = Wasmtime::default();
[278](#278)        r.sizes.fill(resolve);
[279](#279)        r.opts = self.clone();
[280](#280)        r.populate_world_and_interface_options(resolve, world);
[281](#281)        r.generate(resolve, world)
[282](#282)    }
[283](#283)
[284](#284)    fn is_store_data_send(&self) -> bool {
[285](#285)        matches!(self.call_style(), CallStyle::Async | CallStyle::Concurrent)
[286](#286)            || self.require_store_data_send
[287](#287)    }
[288](#288)
[289](#289)    pub fn import_call_style(&self, qualifier: Option<&str>, f: &str) -> CallStyle {
[290](#290)        let matched = |names: &HashSet<String>| {
[291](#291)            names.contains(f)
[292](#292)                || qualifier
[293](#293)                    .map(|v| names.contains(&format!("{v}#{f}")))
[294](#294)                    .unwrap_or(false)
[295](#295)        };
[296](#296)
[297](#297)        match &self.async_ {
[298](#298)            AsyncConfig::AllExceptImports(names) if matched(names) => CallStyle::Sync,
[299](#299)            AsyncConfig::OnlyImports(names) if !matched(names) => CallStyle::Sync,
[300](#300)            _ => self.call_style(),
[301](#301)        }
[302](#302)    }
[303](#303)
[304](#304)    pub fn drop_call_style(&self, qualifier: Option<&str>, r: &str) -> CallStyle {
[305](#305)        self.import_call_style(qualifier, &format!("[drop]{r}"))
[306](#306)    }
[307](#307)
[308](#308)    pub fn call_style(&self) -> CallStyle {
[309](#309)        match &self.async_ {
[310](#310)            AsyncConfig::None => CallStyle::Sync,
[311](#311)
[312](#312)            AsyncConfig::All | AsyncConfig::AllExceptImports(_) | AsyncConfig::OnlyImports(_) => {
[313](#313)                if self.concurrent_imports {
[314](#314)                    CallStyle::Concurrent
[315](#315)                } else {
[316](#316)                    CallStyle::Async
[317](#317)                }
[318](#318)            }
[319](#319)        }
[320](#320)    }

[323](#323)impl Wasmtime {
[324](#324)    fn populate_world_and_interface_options(&mut self, resolve: &Resolve, world: WorldId) {
[325](#325)        self.world_link_options.add_world(resolve, &world);
[326](#326)
[327](#327)        for (_, import) in resolve.worlds[world].imports.iter() {
[328](#328)            match import {
[329](#329)                WorldItem::Interface { id, .. } => {
[330](#330)                    let mut o = LinkOptionsBuilder::default();
[331](#331)                    o.add_interface(resolve, id);
[332](#332)                    self.interface_link_options.insert(*id, o);
[333](#333)                }
[334](#334)                WorldItem::Function(_) | WorldItem::Type(_) => {}
[335](#335)            }
[336](#336)        }
[337](#337)    }
[338](#338)    fn name_interface(
[339](#339)        &mut self,
[340](#340)        resolve: &Resolve,
[341](#341)        id: InterfaceId,
[342](#342)        name: &WorldKey,
[343](#343)        is_export: bool,
[344](#344)    ) -> bool {
[345](#345)        let mut path = Vec::new();
[346](#346)        if is_export {
[347](#347)            path.push("exports".to_string());
[348](#348)        }
[349](#349)        match name {
[350](#350)            WorldKey::Name(name) => {
[351](#351)                path.push(name.to_snake_case());
[352](#352)            }
[353](#353)            WorldKey::Interface(_) => {
[354](#354)                let iface = &resolve.interfaces[id];
[355](#355)                let pkgname = &resolve.packages[iface.package.unwrap()].name;
[356](#356)                path.push(pkgname.namespace.to_snake_case());
[357](#357)                path.push(self.name_package_module(resolve, iface.package.unwrap()));
[358](#358)                path.push(to_rust_ident(iface.name.as_ref().unwrap()));
[359](#359)            }
[360](#360)        }
[361](#361)        let entry = if let Some(name_at_root) = self.lookup_replacement(resolve, name, None) {
[362](#362)            InterfaceName::Remapped {
[363](#363)                name_at_root,
[364](#364)                local_path: path,
[365](#365)            }
[366](#366)        } else {
[367](#367)            InterfaceName::Path(path)
[368](#368)        };
[369](#369)
[370](#370)        let remapped = matches!(entry, InterfaceName::Remapped { .. });
[371](#371)        self.interface_names.insert(id, entry);
[372](#372)        remapped
[373](#373)    }
[374](#374)
[375](#375)    fn name_package_module(&self, resolve: &Resolve, id: PackageId) -> String {
[380](#380)        let pkg = &resolve.packages[id];
[381](#381)        let versions_with_same_name = resolve
[382](#382)            .packages
[383](#383)            .iter()
[384](#384)            .filter_map(|(_, p)| {
[385](#385)                if p.name.namespace == pkg.name.namespace && p.name.name == pkg.name.name {
[386](#386)                    Some(&p.name.version)
[387](#387)                } else {
[388](#388)                    None
[389](#389)                }
[390](#390)            })
[391](#391)            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
[392](#392)        let base = pkg.name.name.to_snake_case();
[393](#393)        if versions_with_same_name.len() == 1 {
[394](#394)            return base;
[395](#395)        }
[396](#396)
[397](#397)        let version = match &pkg.name.version {
[398](#398)            Some(version) => version,
[399](#399)            None => return base,
[403](#403)        };
[404](#404)
[405](#405)        let version = version
[412](#412)            .to_string()
[413](#413)            .replace('.', "_")
[414](#414)            .replace('-', "_")
[415](#415)            .replace('+', "_")
[416](#416)            .to_snake_case();
[417](#417)        format!("{base}{version}")
[418](#418)    }
[419](#419)
[420](#420)    fn generate(&mut self, resolve: &Resolve, id: WorldId) -> anyhow::Result<String> {
[421](#421)        self.types.analyze(resolve, id);
[422](#422)
[423](#423)        self.world_link_options.write_struct(&mut self.src);
[424](#424)
[425](#425)        'outer: for (i, te) in self.opts.trappable_error_type.iter().enumerate() {
[434](#434)            let error_name = format!("_TrappableError{i}");
[435](#435)            for (id, iface) in resolve.interfaces.iter() {
[436](#436)                for (key, projection) in lookup_keys(
[437](#437)                    resolve,
[438](#438)                    &WorldKey::Interface(id),
[439](#439)                    LookupItem::InterfaceNoPop,
[440](#440)                ) {
[441](#441)                    assert!(projection.is_empty());
[442](#442)
[443](#443)                    let suffix = match te.wit_path.strip_prefix(&key) {
[448](#448)                        Some(s) => s,
[449](#449)                        None => continue,
[450](#450)                    };
[451](#451)                    let suffix = match suffix.strip_prefix('/') {
[452](#452)                        Some(s) => s,
[453](#453)                        None => continue,
[454](#454)                    };
[455](#455)                    if let Some(id) = iface.types.get(suffix) {
[456](#456)                        uwriteln!(self.src, "type {error_name} = {};", te.rust_type_name);
[457](#457)                        let prev = self.trappable_errors.insert(*id, error_name);
[458](#458)                        assert!(prev.is_none());
[459](#459)                        continue 'outer;
[460](#460)                    }
[461](#461)                }
[462](#462)            }
[463](#463)
[464](#464)            bail!(
[465](#465)                "failed to locate a WIT error type corresponding to the \
[466](#466)                 `trappable_error_type` name `{}` provided",
[467](#467)                te.wit_path
[468](#468)            )
[469](#469)        }
[470](#470)
[471](#471)        let mut with = self.opts.with.iter_mut().collect::<Vec<_>>();
[476](#476)        with.sort();
[477](#477)        for (i, (_k, v)) in with.into_iter().enumerate() {
[478](#478)            let name = format!("__with_name{i}");
[479](#479)            uwriteln!(self.src, "#[doc(hidden)]\npub use {v} as {name};");
[480](#480)            *v = name;
[481](#481)        }
[482](#482)
[483](#483)        let world = &resolve.worlds[id];
[484](#484)        for (name, import) in world.imports.iter() {
[485](#485)            if !self.opts.only_interfaces || matches!(import, WorldItem::Interface { .. }) {
[486](#486)                self.import(resolve, name, import);
[487](#487)            }
[488](#488)        }
[489](#489)
[490](#490)        for (name, export) in world.exports.iter() {
[491](#491)            if !self.opts.only_interfaces || matches!(export, WorldItem::Interface { .. }) {
[492](#492)                self.export(resolve, name, export);
[493](#493)            }
[494](#494)        }
[495](#495)        self.finish(resolve, id)
[496](#496)    }
[497](#497)
[498](#498)    fn import(&mut self, resolve: &Resolve, name: &WorldKey, item: &WorldItem) {
[499](#499)        let mut generator = InterfaceGenerator::new(self, resolve);
[500](#500)        match item {
[501](#501)            WorldItem::Function(func) => {
[502](#502)                self.import_functions.push(func.clone());
[503](#503)            }
[504](#504)            WorldItem::Interface { id, .. } => {
[505](#505)                generator
[506](#506)                    .generator
[507](#507)                    .interface_last_seen_as_import
[508](#508)                    .insert(*id, true);
[509](#509)                generator.current_interface = Some((*id, name, false));
[510](#510)                let snake = to_rust_ident(&match name {
[511](#511)                    WorldKey::Name(s) => s.to_snake_case(),
[512](#512)                    WorldKey::Interface(id) => resolve.interfaces[*id]
[513](#513)                        .name
[514](#514)                        .as_ref()
[515](#515)                        .unwrap()
[516](#516)                        .to_snake_case(),
[517](#517)                });
[518](#518)                let module = if generator
[519](#519)                    .generator
[520](#520)                    .name_interface(resolve, *id, name, false)
[521](#521)                {
[522](#522)                    let name_at_root = match &generator.generator.interface_names[id] {
[530](#530)                        InterfaceName::Remapped { name_at_root, .. } => name_at_root,
[531](#531)                        InterfaceName::Path(_) => unreachable!(),
[532](#532)                    };
[533](#533)                    let path_to_root = generator.path_to_root();
[534](#534)                    format!(
[535](#535)                        "
[536](#536)                            pub mod {snake} {{
[537](#537)                                #[allow(unused_imports)]
[538](#538)                                pub use {path_to_root}{name_at_root}::*;
[539](#539)                            }}
[540](#540)                        "
[541](#541)                    )
[542](#542)                } else {
[543](#543)                    generator.generator.interface_link_options[id].write_struct(&mut generator.src);
[546](#546)                    generator.types(*id);
[547](#547)                    let key_name = resolve.name_world_key(name);
[548](#548)                    generator.generate_add_to_linker(*id, &key_name);
[549](#549)
[550](#550)                    let module = &generator.src[..];
[551](#551)                    let wt = generator.generator.wasmtime_path();
[552](#552)
[553](#553)                    format!(
[554](#554)                        "
[555](#555)                            #[allow(clippy::all)]
[556](#556)                            pub mod {snake} {{
[557](#557)                                #[allow(unused_imports)]
[558](#558)                                use {wt}::component::__internal::{{anyhow, Box}};
[559](#559)
[560](#560)                                {module}
[561](#561)                            }}
[562](#562)                        "
[563](#563)                    )
[564](#564)                };
[565](#565)                self.import_interfaces.push((
[566](#566)                    name.clone(),
[567](#567)                    *id,
[568](#568)                    module,
[569](#569)                    self.interface_names[id].clone(),
[570](#570)                ));
[571](#571)
[572](#572)                let interface_path = self.import_interface_path(id);
[573](#573)                self.interface_link_options[id]
[574](#574)                    .write_impl_from_world(&mut self.src, &interface_path);
[575](#575)            }
[576](#576)            WorldItem::Type(ty) => {
[577](#577)                let name = match name {
[578](#578)                    WorldKey::Name(name) => name,
[579](#579)                    WorldKey::Interface(_) => unreachable!(),
[580](#580)                };
[581](#581)                generator.define_type(name, *ty);
[582](#582)                let body = mem::take(&mut generator.src);
[583](#583)                self.src.push_str(&body);
[584](#584)            }
[585](#585)        };
[586](#586)    }
[587](#587)
[588](#588)    fn export(&mut self, resolve: &Resolve, name: &WorldKey, item: &WorldItem) {
[589](#589)        let wt = self.wasmtime_path();
[590](#590)        let mut generator = InterfaceGenerator::new(self, resolve);
[591](#591)        let field;
[592](#592)        let ty;
[593](#593)        let ty_index;
[594](#594)        let load;
[595](#595)        let get_index;
[596](#596)        match item {
[597](#597)            WorldItem::Function(func) => {
[598](#598)                generator.define_rust_guest_export(resolve, None, func);
[599](#599)                let body = mem::take(&mut generator.src).into();
[600](#600)                load = generator.extract_typed_function(func).1;
[601](#601)                assert!(generator.src.is_empty());
[602](#602)                generator.generator.exports.funcs.push(body);
[603](#603)                ty_index = format!("{wt}::component::ComponentExportIndex");
[604](#604)                field = func_field_name(resolve, func);
[605](#605)                ty = format!("{wt}::component::Func");
[606](#606)                let sig = generator.typedfunc_sig(func, TypeMode::AllBorrowed("'_"));
[607](#607)                let typecheck = format!(
[608](#608)                    "match item {{
[609](#609)                            {wt}::component::types::ComponentItem::ComponentFunc(func) => {{
[610](#610)                                anyhow::Context::context(
[611](#611)                                    func.typecheck::<{sig}>(&_instance_type),
[612](#612)                                    \"type-checking export func `{0}`\"
[613](#613)                                )?;
[614](#614)                                index
[615](#615)                            }}
[616](#616)                            _ => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"export `{0}` is not a function\"))?,
[617](#617)                        }}",
[618](#618)                    func.name
[619](#619)                );
[620](#620)                get_index = format!(
[621](#621)                    "{{ let (item, index) = _component.get_export(None, \"{}\")
[622](#622)                        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"no export `{0}` found\"))?;
[623](#623)                        {typecheck}
[624](#624)                     }}",
[625](#625)                    func.name
[626](#626)                );
[627](#627)            }
[628](#628)            WorldItem::Type(_) => unreachable!(),
[629](#629)            WorldItem::Interface { id, .. } => {
[630](#630)                generator
[631](#631)                    .generator
[632](#632)                    .interface_last_seen_as_import
[633](#633)                    .insert(*id, false);
[634](#634)                generator.generator.name_interface(resolve, *id, name, true);
[635](#635)                generator.current_interface = Some((*id, name, true));
[636](#636)                generator.types(*id);
[637](#637)                let struct_name = "Guest";
[638](#638)                let iface = &resolve.interfaces[*id];
[639](#639)                let iface_name = match name {
[640](#640)                    WorldKey::Name(name) => name,
[641](#641)                    WorldKey::Interface(_) => iface.name.as_ref().unwrap(),
[642](#642)                };
[643](#643)                uwriteln!(generator.src, "pub struct {struct_name} {{");
[644](#644)                for (_, func) in iface.functions.iter() {
[645](#645)                    uwriteln!(
[646](#646)                        generator.src,
[647](#647)                        "{}: {wt}::component::Func,",
[648](#648)                        func_field_name(resolve, func)
[649](#649)                    );
[650](#650)                }
[651](#651)                uwriteln!(generator.src, "}}");
[652](#652)
[653](#653)                uwriteln!(generator.src, "#[derive(Clone)]");
[654](#654)                uwriteln!(generator.src, "pub struct {struct_name}Indices {{");
[655](#655)                for (_, func) in iface.functions.iter() {
[656](#656)                    uwriteln!(
[657](#657)                        generator.src,
[658](#658)                        "{}: {wt}::component::ComponentExportIndex,",
[659](#659)                        func_field_name(resolve, func)
[660](#660)                    );
[661](#661)                }

[663](#663)

[665](#665)                let instance_name = resolve.name_world_key(name);
[666](#666)                uwrite!(
[667](#667)                    generator.src,
[668](#668)                    "

[675](#675)pub fn new<_T>(

[677](#677)) -> {wt}::Result<{struct_name}Indices> {{

[680](#680)    let mut lookup = move |name| {{

[825](#825)            field,
[826](#826)            ExportField {
[827](#827)                ty,
[828](#828)                ty_index,

[834](#834)    }

[836](#836)    fn build_world_struct(&mut self, resolve: &Resolve, world: WorldId) {
[837](#837)        let wt = self.wasmtime_path();
[838](#838)        let world_name = &resolve.worlds[world].name;
[839](#839)        let camel = to_rust_upper_camel_case(&world_name);
[840](#840)        let (async_, async__, where_clause, await_) = match self.opts.call_style() {

[842](#842)                ("async", "_async", "where _T: Send", ".await")

[847](#847)            self.src,

[860](#860)}}

[866](#866)            indices: self.indices.clone(),
[867](#867)        }}

[878](#878)        let indices = {camel}Indices::new(&instance_pre)?;
[879](#879)        Ok(Self {{ instance_pre, indices }})

[890](#890)    /// Instantiates a new instance of [`{camel}`] within the

[896](#896)    /// resulting instance.

[898](#898)        &self,

[901](#901)        {where_clause}

[905](#905)        self.indices.load(&mut store, &instance)
[906](#906)    }}

[909](#909)        );

[911](#911)        uwriteln!(
[912](#912)            self.src,
[913](#913)            "
[914](#914)            /// Auto-generated bindings for index of the exports of

[931](#931)            "
[932](#932)                /// Auto-generated bindings for an instance a component which
[933](#933)                /// implements the world `{world_name}`.
[934](#934)                ///
[935](#935)                /// This structure can be created through a number of means
[936](#936)                /// depending on your requirements and what you have on hand:
[937](#937)                ///
[938](#938)                /// * The most convenient way is to use
[939](#939)                ///   [`{camel}::instantiate{async__}`] which only needs a
[940](#940)                ///   [`Store`], [`Component`], and [`Linker`].
[941](#941)                ///
[942](#942)                /// * Alternatively you can create a [`{camel}Pre`] ahead of
[943](#943)                ///   time with a [`Component`] to front-load string lookups
[944](#944)                ///   of exports once instead of per-instantiation. This
[945](#945)                ///   method then uses [`{camel}Pre::instantiate{async__}`] to
[946](#946)                ///   create a [`{camel}`].
[947](#947)                ///
[948](#948)                /// * If you've instantiated the instance yourself already
[949](#949)                ///   then you can use [`{camel}::new`].
[950](#950)                ///
[951](#951)                /// These methods are all equivalent to one another and move
[952](#952)                /// around the tradeoff of what work is performed when.
[953](#953)                ///
[954](#954)                /// [`Store`]: {wt}::Store
[955](#955)                /// [`Component`]: {wt}::component::Component
[956](#956)                /// [`Linker`]: {wt}::component::Linker
[957](#957)                pub struct {camel} {{"
[958](#958)        );

[960](#960)            uwriteln!(self.src, "{name}: {},", field.ty);
[961](#961)        }

[963](#963)
[964](#964)        let world_trait = self.world_imports_trait(resolve, world);
[965](#965)
[966](#966)        uwriteln!(self.src, "const _: () = {{");
[967](#967)        uwriteln!(
[968](#968)            self.src,
[969](#969)            "
[970](#970)                #[allow(unused_imports)]
[971](#971)                use {wt}::component::__internal::anyhow;
[972](#972)            "
[973](#973)        );
[974](#974)
[975](#975)        uwriteln!(
[976](#976)            self.src,
[977](#977)            "impl {camel}Indices {{
[978](#978)                /// Creates a new copy of `{camel}Indices` bindings which can then
[979](#979)                /// be used to instantiate into a particular store.
[980](#980)                ///
[981](#981)                /// This method may fail if the component does not have the
[982](#982)                /// required exports.
[983](#983)                pub fn new<_T>(_instance_pre: &{wt}::component::InstancePre<_T>) -> {wt}::Result<Self> {{
[984](#984)                    let _component = _instance_pre.component();
[985](#985)                    let _instance_type = _instance_pre.instance_type();
[986](#986)            ",
[987](#987)        );
[988](#988)        for (name, field) in self.exports.fields.iter() {

[996](#996)        uwriteln!(self.src, "}}"); uwriteln!(
[999](#999)            self.src,

[1001](#1001)                /// Uses the indices stored in `self` to load an instance

[1007](#1007)                    &self,

[1017](#1017)        }

[1019](#1019)        for (name, _) in self.exports.fields.iter() {
[1020](#1020)            uwriteln!(self.src, "{name},");
[1021](#1021)        }

[1023](#1023)        uwriteln!(self.src, "}}"); uwriteln!(self.src, "}}"); uwriteln!(
