[2712](#2712)    fn define_rust_guest_export(
[2713](#2713)        &mut self,
[2714](#2714)        resolve: &Resolve,
[2715](#2715)        ns: Option<&WorldKey>,
[2716](#2716)        func: &Function,
[2717](#2717)    ) {
[2718](#2718)        let style = self.generator.opts.call_style();
[2721](#2721)        let (async_, async__, await_, concurrent) = match &style {
[2722](#2722)            CallStyle::Async | CallStyle::Concurrent => {
[2723](#2723)                if self.generator.opts.concurrent_exports {
[2724](#2724)                    ("", "INVALID", "INVALID", true)
[2725](#2725)                } else {
[2726](#2726)                    ("async", "_async", ".await", false)
[2727](#2727)                }
[2728](#2728)            }
[2729](#2729)            CallStyle::Sync => ("", "", "", false),
[2730](#2730)        };
[2731](#2731)
[2732](#2732)        self.rustdoc(&func.docs);
[2733](#2733)        let wt = self.generator.wasmtime_path();
[2734](#2734)
[2735](#2735)        uwrite!(
[2736](#2736)            self.src,
[2737](#2737)            "pub {async_} fn call_{}<S: {wt}::AsContextMut>(&self, mut store: S, ",
[2738](#2738)            func.item_name().to_snake_case(),
[2739](#2739)        );
[2740](#2740)
[2741](#2741)        let param_mode = if let CallStyle::Concurrent = &style {
[2742](#2742)            TypeMode::Owned
[2743](#2743)        } else {
[2744](#2744)            TypeMode::AllBorrowed("'_")
[2745](#2745)        };
[2746](#2746)
[2747](#2747)        for (i, param) in func.params.iter().enumerate() {
[2748](#2748)            uwrite!(self.src, "arg{}: ", i);
[2749](#2749)            self.print_ty(¶m.1, param_mode);
[2750](#2750)            self.push_str(",");
[2751](#2751)        }
[2752](#2752)
[2753](#2753)        if concurrent {
[2754](#2754)            uwrite!(
[2755](#2755)                self.src,
[2756](#2756)                ") -> impl {wt}::component::__internal::Future<Output = {wt}::Result<"
[2757](#2757)            );
[2758](#2758)        } else {
[2759](#2759)            uwrite!(self.src, ") -> {wt}::Result<");
[2760](#2760)        }
[2761](#2761)        self.print_result_ty(func.result, TypeMode::Owned);
[2762](#2762)        if concurrent {
[2763](#2763)            uwrite!(self.src, ">> + Send + 'static + use<S>");
[2764](#2764)        } else {
[2765](#2765)            uwrite!(self.src, ">");
[2766](#2766)        }
[2767](#2767)
[2768](#2768)        match style {
[2769](#2769)            CallStyle::Concurrent => {
[2770](#2770)                uwrite!(
[2771](#2771)                    self.src,
[2772](#2772)                    " where <S as {wt}::AsContext>::Data: Send + 'static",
[2773](#2773)                );
[2774](#2774)            }
[2775](#2775)            CallStyle::Async => {
[2776](#2776)                uwrite!(self.src, " where <S as {wt}::AsContext>::Data: Send");
[2777](#2777)            }
[2778](#2778)            CallStyle::Sync => {}
[2779](#2779)        }
[2780](#2780)        uwrite!(self.src, "{{\n");
[2781](#2781)
[2782](#2782)        if self.generator.opts.tracing && !concurrent {
[2784](#2784)            if let CallStyle::Async | CallStyle::Concurrent = &style {
[2785](#2785)                self.src.push_str("use tracing::Instrument;\n");
[2786](#2786)            }
[2787](#2787)
[2788](#2788)            let ns = match ns {
[2789](#2789)                Some(key) => resolve.name_world_key(key),
[2790](#2790)                None => "default".to_string(),
[2791](#2791)            };
[2792](#2792)            self.src.push_str(&format!(
[2793](#2793)                "
[2794](#2794)                   let span = tracing::span!(
[2795](#2795)                       tracing::Level::TRACE,
[2796](#2796)                       \"wit-bindgen export\",
[2797](#2797)                       module = \"{ns}\",
[2798](#2798)                       function = \"{}\",
[2799](#2799)                   );
[2800](#2800)               ",
[2801](#2801)                func.name,
[2802](#2802)            ));
[2803](#2803)
[2804](#2804)            if !matches!(&style, CallStyle::Async | CallStyle::Concurrent) {
[2805](#2805)                self.src.push_str(
[2806](#2806)                    "
[2807](#2807)                   let _enter = span.enter();
[2808](#2808)                   ",
[2809](#2809)                );
[2810](#2810)            }
[2811](#2811)        }
[2812](#2812)
[2813](#2813)        self.src.push_str("let callee = unsafe {\n");
[2814](#2814)        uwrite!(
[2815](#2815)            self.src,
[2816](#2816)            "{wt}::component::TypedFunc::<{}>",
[2817](#2817)            self.typedfunc_sig(func, param_mode)
[2818](#2818)        );
[2819](#2819)        let projection_to_func = if func.kind.resource().is_some() {
[2820](#2820)            ".funcs"
[2821](#2821)        } else {
[2822](#2822)            ""
[2823](#2823)        };
[2824](#2824)        uwriteln!(
[2825](#2825)            self.src,
[2826](#2826)            "::new_unchecked(self{projection_to_func}.{})",
[2827](#2827)            func_field_name(self.resolve, func),
[2828](#2828)        );
[2829](#2829)        self.src.push_str("};\n");
[2830](#2830)
[2831](#2831)        if concurrent {
[2832](#2832)            if func.result.is_some() {
[2833](#2833)                uwrite!(self.src, "{wt}::component::__internal::FutureExt::map(");
[2834](#2834)            }
[2835](#2835)            uwrite!(self.src, "callee.call_concurrent(store.as_context_mut(), (");
[2836](#2836)            for (i, _) in func.params.iter().enumerate() {
[2837](#2837)                uwrite!(self.src, "arg{i}, ");
[2838](#2838)            }
[2839](#2839)            self.src.push_str("))");
[2840](#2840)
[2841](#2841)            if func.result.is_some() {
[2842](#2842)                self.src.push_str(", |v| v.map(|(v,)| v))");
[2843](#2843)            }
[2844](#2844)        } else {
[2845](#2845)            self.src.push_str("let (");
[2846](#2846)            if func.result.is_some() {
[2847](#2847)                uwrite!(self.src, "ret0,");
[2848](#2848)            }
[2849](#2849)            uwrite!(
[2850](#2850)                self.src,
[2851](#2851)                ") = callee.call{async__}(store.as_context_mut(), ("
[2852](#2852)            );
[2853](#2853)            for (i, _) in func.params.iter().enumerate() {
[2854](#2854)                uwrite!(self.src, "arg{}, ", i);
[2855](#2855)            }
[2856](#2856)
[2857](#2857)            let instrument = if matches!(&style, CallStyle::Async | CallStyle::Concurrent)
[2858](#2858)                && self.generator.opts.tracing
[2859](#2859)            {
[2860](#2860)                ".instrument(span.clone())"
[2861](#2861)            } else {
[2862](#2862)                ""
[2863](#2863)            };
[2864](#2864)            uwriteln!(self.src, ")){instrument}{await_}?;");
[2865](#2865)
[2866](#2866)            let instrument = if matches!(&style, CallStyle::Async | CallStyle::Concurrent)
[2867](#2867)                && self.generator.opts.tracing
[2868](#2868)            {
[2869](#2869)                ".instrument(span)"
[2870](#2870)            } else {
[2871](#2871)                ""
[2872](#2872)            };
[2873](#2873)
[2874](#2874)            uwriteln!(
[2875](#2875)                self.src,
[2876](#2876)                "callee.post_return{async__}(store.as_context_mut()){instrument}{await_}?;"
[2877](#2877)            );
[2878](#2878)
[2879](#2879)            self.src.push_str("Ok(");
[2880](#2880)            if func.result.is_some() {
[2881](#2881)                self.src.push_str("ret0");
[2882](#2882)            } else {

[2884](#2884)            }

[2887](#2887)
[2888](#2888)        self.src.push_str("}\n");
[2890](#2890)    }
[2891](#2891)
[2892](#2892)    fn rustdoc(&mut self, docs: &Docs) {
[2893](#2893)        let docs = match &docs.contents {
[2894](#2894)            Some(docs) => docs,
[2895](#2895)            None => return,
[2896](#2896)        };
[2897](#2897)        for line in docs.trim().lines() {
[2898](#2898)            self.push_str("/// ");
[2899](#2899)            self.push_str(line);
[2900](#2900)            self.push_str("\n");
[2901](#2901)        }
[2902](#2902)    }
[2903](#2903)
[2904](#2904)    fn path_to_root(&self) -> String {
[2905](#2905)        let mut path_to_root = String::new();
[2906](#2906)        if let Some((_, key, is_export)) = self.current_interface {
[2907](#2907)            match key {
[2908](#2908)                WorldKey::Name(_) => {
[2909](#2909)                    path_to_root.push_str("super::");
[2910](#2910)                }
[2911](#2911)                WorldKey::Interface(_) => {
[2912](#2912)                    path_to_root.push_str("super::super::super::");
[2913](#2913)                }
[2914](#2914)            }
[2915](#2915)            if is_export {
[2916](#2916)                path_to_root.push_str("super::");
[2917](#2917)            }
[2918](#2918)        }
[2919](#2919)        path_to_root
[2920](#2920)    }
[2921](#2921)
[2922](#2922)    fn import_call_style(&self, func: &Function) -> CallStyle {
[2923](#2923)        self.generator
[2924](#2924)            .opts
[2925](#2925)            .import_call_style(self.qualifier().as_deref(), &func.name)
[2926](#2926)    }
[2927](#2927)
[2928](#2928)    fn partition_concurrent_funcs<'b>(
[2929](#2929)        &self,
[2930](#2930)        funcs: impl IntoIterator<Item = &'b Function>,
[2931](#2931)    ) -> FunctionPartitioning<'b> {
[2932](#2932)        let (concurrent, sync) =
[2933](#2933)            funcs
[2934](#2934)                .into_iter()
[2935](#2935)                .partition(|func| match self.import_call_style(func) {
[2936](#2936)                    CallStyle::Concurrent => true,
[2937](#2937)                    CallStyle::Async | CallStyle::Sync => false,
[2938](#2938)                });
[2939](#2939)        FunctionPartitioning { concurrent, sync }
[2940](#2940)    }
[2941](#2941)
[2942](#2942)    fn generate_trait(
[2943](#2943)        &mut self,
[2944](#2944)        trait_name: &str,
[2945](#2945)        functions: &[&Function],
[2946](#2946)        extra_functions: &[ExtraTraitMethod<'_>],
[2947](#2947)        resources: &[(TypeId, &str)],
[2948](#2948)    ) -> GeneratedTrait {
[2949](#2949)        let mut ret = GeneratedTrait::default();
[2950](#2950)        let wt = self.generator.wasmtime_path();
[2951](#2951)        let is_maybe_async = matches!(
[2952](#2952)            self.generator.opts.call_style(),
[2953](#2953)            CallStyle::Async | CallStyle::Concurrent
[2954](#2954)        );
[2955](#2955)        let partition = self.partition_concurrent_funcs(functions.iter().copied());
[2956](#2956)        ret.any_concurrent = !partition.concurrent.is_empty();
[2957](#2957)
[2958](#2958)        let mut concurrent_supertraits = vec![format!("{wt}::component::HasData")];
[2959](#2959)        let mut sync_supertraits = vec![];
[2960](#2960)        if is_maybe_async {
[2961](#2961)            concurrent_supertraits.push("Send".to_string());
[2962](#2962)            sync_supertraits.push("Send".to_string());
[2963](#2963)        }
[2964](#2964)        for (id, name) in resources {
[2965](#2965)            let camel = name.to_upper_camel_case();
[2966](#2966)            sync_supertraits.push(format!("Host{camel}"));
[2967](#2967)            let funcs = self.partition_concurrent_funcs(get_resource_functions(self.resolve, *id));
[2968](#2968)            if !funcs.concurrent.is_empty() {
[2969](#2969)                ret.any_concurrent = true;
[2970](#2970)                concurrent_supertraits.push(format!("Host{camel}Concurrent"));
[2971](#2971)            }
[2972](#2972)        }
[2973](#2973)
[2974](#2974)        if ret.any_concurrent {
[2975](#2975)            uwriteln!(
[2976](#2976)                self.src,
[2977](#2977)                "#[{wt}::component::__internal::trait_variant_make(::core::marker::Send)]",
[2978](#2978)            );
[2979](#2979)            uwriteln!(
[2980](#2980)                self.src,
[2981](#2981)                "pub trait {trait_name}Concurrent: {} {{",
[2982](#2982)                concurrent_supertraits.join(" + "),
[2983](#2983)            );
[2984](#2984)            ret.concurrent_name = Some(format!("{trait_name}Concurrent"));
[2985](#2985)            for func in partition.concurrent.iter() {
[2986](#2986)                self.generate_function_trait_sig(func, false);
[2987](#2987)                self.push_str(";\n");
[2988](#2988)            }
[2989](#2989)            uwriteln!(self.src, "}}");
[2990](#2990)        }
[2991](#2991)
[2992](#2992)        if is_maybe_async {
[2993](#2993)            uwriteln!(
[2994](#2994)                self.src,
[2995](#2995)                "#[{wt}::component::__internal::trait_variant_make(::core::marker::Send)]",
[2996](#2996)            );
[2997](#2997)        }
[2998](#2998)        uwriteln!(
[2999](#2999)            self.src,
[3000](#3000)            "pub trait {trait_name}: {} {{",
[3001](#3001)            sync_supertraits.join(" + ")
[3002](#3002)        );
[3003](#3003)        ret.name = trait_name.to_string();
[3004](#3004)        for func in partition.sync.iter() {
[3005](#3005)            self.generate_function_trait_sig(func, false);
[3006](#3006)            self.push_str(";\n");
[3007](#3007)        }
[3008](#3008)
[3009](#3009)        for extra in extra_functions {
[3010](#3010)            match extra {
[3011](#3011)                ExtraTraitMethod::ResourceDrop { name } => {
[3012](#3012)                    let camel = name.to_upper_camel_case();
[3013](#3013)                    if let CallStyle::Async | CallStyle::Concurrent = self
[3014](#3014)                        .generator
[3015](#3015)                        .opts
[3016](#3016)                        .drop_call_style(self.qualifier().as_deref(), name)
[3017](#3017)                    {
[3018](#3018)                        uwrite!(self.src, "async ");
[3019](#3019)                    }
[3020](#3020)                    uwrite!(
[3021](#3021)                        self.src,
[3022](#3022)                        "fn drop(&mut self, rep: {wt}::component::Resource<{camel}>) -> {wt}::Result<()>;"
[3023](#3023)                    );
[3024](#3024)                }
[3025](#3025)                ExtraTraitMethod::ErrorConvert { name, id } => {
[3026](#3026)                    let root = self.path_to_root();
[3027](#3027)                    let custom_name = &self.generator.trappable_errors[id];
[3028](#3028)                    let snake = name.to_snake_case();
[3029](#3029)                    let camel = name.to_upper_camel_case();
[3030](#3030)                    uwriteln!(
[3031](#3031)                        self.src,
[3032](#3032)                        "
[3033](#3033)fn convert_{snake}(&mut self, err: {root}{custom_name}) -> {wt}::Result<{camel}>;
[3034](#3034)                        "
[3035](#3035)                    );
[3036](#3036)                }
[3037](#3037)            }
[3038](#3038)        }
[3039](#3039)
[3040](#3040)        uwriteln!(self.src, "}}");
[3041](#3041)
[3042](#3042)        if self.generator.opts.skip_mut_forwarding_impls {
[3043](#3043)            return ret;
[3044](#3044)        }
[3045](#3045)
[3046](#3046)        let maybe_send = if is_maybe_async { "+ Send" } else { "" };
[3048](#3048)        uwriteln!(
[3049](#3049)            self.src,
[3050](#3050)            "impl <_T: {trait_name} + ?Sized {maybe_send}> {trait_name} for &mut _T {{"
[3051](#3051)        );
[3052](#3052)        for func in partition.sync.iter() {
[3053](#3053)            let call_style = self.import_call_style(func);
[3054](#3054)            self.generate_function_trait_sig(func, true);
[3055](#3055)            uwrite!(
[3056](#3056)                self.src,
[3057](#3057)                "{{ {trait_name}::{}(*self,",
[3058](#3058)                rust_function_name(func)
[3059](#3059)            );
[3060](#3060)            for (name, _) in func.params.iter() {
[3061](#3061)                uwrite!(self.src, "{},", to_rust_ident(name));
[3062](#3062)            }
[3063](#3063)            uwrite!(self.src, ")");
[3064](#3064)            if let CallStyle::Async = &call_style {
[3065](#3065)                uwrite!(self.src, ".await");
[3066](#3066)            }
[3067](#3067)            uwriteln!(self.src, "}}");
[3068](#3068)        }
[3069](#3069)        for extra in extra_functions {
[3070](#3070)            match extra {
[3071](#3071)                ExtraTraitMethod::ResourceDrop { name } => {
[3072](#3072)                    let camel = name.to_upper_camel_case();
[3073](#3073)                    let mut await_ = "";
[3074](#3074)                    if let CallStyle::Async | CallStyle::Concurrent = self
[3075](#3075)                        .generator
[3076](#3076)                        .opts
[3077](#3077)                        .drop_call_style(self.qualifier().as_deref(), name)
[3078](#3078)                    {
[3079](#3079)                        self.src.push_str("async ");
[3080](#3080)                        await_ = ".await";
[3081](#3081)                    }
[3082](#3082)                    uwriteln!(
[3083](#3083)                        self.src,
[3084](#3084)                        "
[3085](#3085)fn drop(&mut self, rep: {wt}::component::Resource<{camel}>) -> {wt}::Result<()> {{
[3086](#3086)    {trait_name}::drop(*self, rep){await_}
[3087](#3087)}}
[3088](#3088)                        ",
[3089](#3089)                    );
[3090](#3090)                }
[3091](#3091)                ExtraTraitMethod::ErrorConvert { name, id } => {
[3092](#3092)                    let root = self.path_to_root();
[3093](#3093)                    let custom_name = &self.generator.trappable_errors[id];
[3094](#3094)                    let snake = name.to_snake_case();
[3095](#3095)                    let camel = name.to_upper_camel_case();
[3096](#3096)                    uwriteln!(
[3097](#3097)                        self.src,
[3098](#3098)                        "
[3099](#3099)fn convert_{snake}(&mut self, err: {root}{custom_name}) -> {wt}::Result<{camel}> {{
[3100](#3100)    {trait_name}::convert_{snake}(*self, err)
[3101](#3101)}}
[3102](#3102)                        ",
[3103](#3103)                    );
[3104](#3104)                }
[3105](#3105)            }
[3106](#3106)        }
[3107](#3107)        uwriteln!(self.src, "}}");
[3108](#3108)
[3109](#3109)        ret
[3110](#3110)    }
[3111](#3111)}

[3141](#3141)            if cur == interface {
[3142](#3142)                return None;
[3143](#3143)            }
[3144](#3144)        }

[3181](#3181)impl LinkOptionsBuilder {
[3182](#3182)    fn has_any(&self) -> bool {
[3183](#3183)        !self.unstable_features.is_empty()
[3184](#3184)    }
[3185](#3185)    fn add_world(&mut self, resolve: &Resolve, id: &WorldId) {
[3186](#3186)        let world = &resolve.worlds[*id];
[3187](#3187)
[3188](#3188)        self.add_stability(&world.stability);
[3189](#3189)
[3190](#3190)        for (_, import) in world.imports.iter() {
[3191](#3191)            match import {
[3192](#3192)                WorldItem::Interface { id, stability } => {
[3193](#3193)                    self.add_stability(stability);
[3194](#3194)                    self.add_interface(resolve, id);
[3195](#3195)                }
[3196](#3196)                WorldItem::Function(f) => {
[3197](#3197)                    self.add_stability(&f.stability);
[3198](#3198)                }
[3199](#3199)                WorldItem::Type(t) => {
[3200](#3200)                    self.add_type(resolve, t);
[3201](#3201)                }
[3202](#3202)            }
[3203](#3203)        }
[3204](#3204)    }
[3205](#3205)    fn add_interface(&mut self, resolve: &Resolve, id: &InterfaceId) {
[3206](#3206)        let interface = &resolve.interfaces[*id];
[3207](#3207)
[3208](#3208)        self.add_stability(&interface.stability);
[3209](#3209)
[3210](#3210)        for (_, t) in interface.types.iter() {
[3211](#3211)            self.add_type(resolve, t);
[3212](#3212)        }
[3213](#3213)        for (_, f) in interface.functions.iter() {
[3214](#3214)            self.add_stability(&f.stability);
[3215](#3215)        }
[3216](#3216)    }
[3217](#3217)    fn add_type(&mut self, resolve: &Resolve, id: &TypeId) {
[3218](#3218)        let t = &resolve.types[*id];
[3219](#3219)        self.add_stability(&t.stability);
[3220](#3220)    }
[3221](#3221)    fn add_stability(&mut self, stability: &Stability) {
[3222](#3222)        match stability {
[3223](#3223)            Stability::Unstable { feature, .. } => {
[3224](#3224)                self.unstable_features.insert(feature.clone());
[3225](#3225)            }
[3226](#3226)            Stability::Stable { .. } | Stability::Unknown => {}
[3227](#3227)        }
[3228](#3228)    }
[3229](#3229)    fn write_struct(&self, src: &mut Source) {
[3230](#3230)        if !self.has_any() {
[3231](#3231)            return;
[3232](#3232)        }
[3233](#3233)
[3234](#3234)        let mut unstable_features = self.unstable_features.iter().cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>();
[3235](#3235)        unstable_features.sort();
[3236](#3236)
[3237](#3237)        uwriteln!(
[3238](#3238)            src,
[3239](#3239)            "
[3240](#3240)            /// Link-time configurations.
[3241](#3241)            #[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
[3242](#3242)            pub struct LinkOptions {{
[3243](#3243)            "
[3244](#3244)        );

[3247](#3247)            let feature_rust_name = feature.to_snake_case();
[3248](#3248)            uwriteln!(src, "{feature_rust_name}: bool,");
[3249](#3249)        }
[3250](#3250)
[3251](#3251)        uwriteln!(src, "}}");
[3252](#3252)        uwriteln!(src, "impl LinkOptions {{");
[3253](#3253)
[3254](#3254)        for feature in unstable_features.iter() {
[3255](#3255)            let feature_rust_name = feature.to_snake_case();
[3256](#3256)            uwriteln!(
[3257](#3257)                src,
[3258](#3258)                "
[3259](#3259)                /// Enable members marked as `@unstable(feature = {feature})`
[3260](#3260)                pub fn {feature_rust_name}(&mut self, enabled: bool) -> &mut Self {{
[3261](#3261)                    self.{feature_rust_name} = enabled;
[3262](#3262)                    self

[3267](#3267)
[3268](#3268)        uwriteln!(src, "}}");
[3269](#3269)    }
[3270](#3270)    fn write_impl_from_world(&self, src: &mut Source, path: &str) {
[3271](#3271)        if !self.has_any() {
[3272](#3272)            return;

[3289](#3289)                    let mut dest = Self::default();
[3290](#3290)        "

[3315](#3315)            let feature_rust_name = feature.to_snake_case();
[3316](#3316)            uwrite!(src, "if options.{feature_rust_name} {{");
[3317](#3317)            true
[3318](#3318)        } else {
[3319](#3319)            false
[3320](#3320)        };
[3321](#3321)        Self { close }
[3322](#3322)    }
[3323](#3323)
[3324](#3324)    fn close(self, src: &mut Source) {
[3325](#3325)        if self.close {
[3326](#3326)            uwriteln!(src, "}}");
[3327](#3327)        }

[3331](#3331)fn formatting_for_arg(
[3333](#3333)    name: &str,
[3334](#3334)    index: usize,
[3335](#3335)    ty: Type,
[3336](#3336)    opts: &Opts,
[3337](#3337)    resolve: &Resolve,
[3338](#3338)) -> String {
[3339](#3339)    if !opts.verbose_tracing && type_contains_lists(ty, resolve) {
[3340](#3340)        return format!("{name} = tracing::field::debug(\"...\")");
[3341](#3341)    }
[3342](#3342)
[3343](#3343)    format!("{name} = tracing::field::debug(&arg{index})")
[3345](#3345)}
[3346](#3346)
[3347](#3347)fn formatting_for_results(result: Option<Type>, opts: &Opts, resolve: &Resolve) -> String {
[3349](#3349)    let contains_lists = match result {
[3350](#3350)        Some(ty) => type_contains_lists(ty, resolve),
[3351](#3351)        None => false,
[3352](#3352)    };
[3353](#3353)
[3354](#3354)    if !opts.verbose_tracing && contains_lists {
[3355](#3355)        return format!("result = tracing::field::debug(\"...\")");
[3356](#3356)    }
[3357](#3357)
[3358](#3358)    format!("result = tracing::field::debug(&r)")
[3360](#3360)}
[3361](#3361)
[3362](#3362)fn type_contains_lists(ty: Type, resolve: &Resolve) -> bool {
[3366](#3366)    match ty {
[3367](#3367)        Type::Id(id) => match &resolve.types[id].kind {
[3368](#3368)            TypeDefKind::Resource
[3369](#3369)            | TypeDefKind::Unknown
[3370](#3370)            | TypeDefKind::Flags(_)
[3371](#3371)            | TypeDefKind::Handle(_)
[3372](#3372)            | TypeDefKind::Enum(_)
[3373](#3373)            | TypeDefKind::Stream(_)
[3374](#3374)            | TypeDefKind::Future(_) => false,
[3375](#3375)            TypeDefKind::Option(ty) => type_contains_lists(*ty, resolve),
[3376](#3376)            TypeDefKind::Result(Result_ { ok, err }) => {
[3377](#3377)                option_type_contains_lists(*ok, resolve)
[3378](#3378)                    || option_type_contains_lists(*err, resolve)
[3379](#3379)            }
[3380](#3380)            TypeDefKind::Record(record) => record
[3381](#3381)                .fields
[3382](#3382)                .iter()
[3383](#3383)                .any(|field| type_contains_lists(field.ty, resolve)),
[3384](#3384)            TypeDefKind::Tuple(tuple) => tuple
[3385](#3385)                .types
[3386](#3386)                .iter()
[3387](#3387)                .any(|ty| type_contains_lists(*ty, resolve)),
[3388](#3388)            TypeDefKind::Variant(variant) => variant
[3389](#3389)                .cases
[3390](#3390)                .iter()
[3391](#3391)                .any(|case| option_type_contains_lists(case.ty, resolve)),
[3392](#3392)            TypeDefKind::Type(ty) => type_contains_lists(*ty, resolve),
[3393](#3393)            TypeDefKind::List(_) => true,
[3394](#3394)            TypeDefKind::FixedSizeList(..) => todo!(),
[3395](#3395)        },
[3396](#3396)
[3397](#3397)        _ => false,
[3400](#3400)    }
[3401](#3401)}
[3402](#3402)
[3403](#3403)fn option_type_contains_lists(ty: Option<Type>, resolve: &Resolve) -> bool {
[3404](#3404)    match ty {
[3405](#3405)        Some(ty) => type_contains_lists(ty, resolve),
[3406](#3406)        None => false,
[3407](#3407)    }
[3408](#3408)}
[3409](#3409)
[3410](#3410)fn resolve_type_definition_id(resolve: &Resolve, mut id: TypeId) -> TypeId {
[3414](#3414)    loop {
[3415](#3415)        match resolve.types[id].kind {
[3416](#3416)            TypeDefKind::Type(Type::Id(def_id)) => id = def_id,
[3417](#3417)            _ => return id,
[3418](#3418)        }
[3419](#3419)    }
[3420](#3420)}
[3421](#3421)
[3422](#3422)fn rust_function_name(func: &Function) -> String {
[3423](#3423)    match func.kind {
[3424](#3424)        FunctionKind::Constructor(_) => "new".to_string(),
[3425](#3425)        FunctionKind::Method(_)
[3426](#3426)        | FunctionKind::Static(_)
[3427](#3427)        | FunctionKind::AsyncMethod(_)
[3428](#3428)        | FunctionKind::AsyncStatic(_)
[3429](#3429)        | FunctionKind::Freestanding
[3430](#3430)        | FunctionKind::AsyncFreestanding => to_rust_ident(func.item_name()),
[3431](#3431)    }
[3432](#3432)}
[3433](#3433)
[3434](#3434)fn func_field_name(resolve: &Resolve, func: &Function) -> String {
[3435](#3435)    let mut name = String::new();
[3436](#3436)    match func.kind {
[3437](#3437)        FunctionKind::Method(id) | FunctionKind::AsyncMethod(id) => {
[3438](#3438)            name.push_str("method-");
[3439](#3439)            name.push_str(resolve.types[id].name.as_ref().unwrap());
[3440](#3440)            name.push_str("-");
[3441](#3441)        }
[3442](#3442)        FunctionKind::Static(id) | FunctionKind::AsyncStatic(id) => {
[3443](#3443)            name.push_str("static-");
[3444](#3444)            name.push_str(resolve.types[id].name.as_ref().unwrap());
[3445](#3445)            name.push_str("-");
[3446](#3446)        }
[3447](#3447)        FunctionKind::Constructor(id) => {
[3448](#3448)            name.push_str("constructor-");
[3449](#3449)            name.push_str(resolve.types[id].name.as_ref().unwrap());
[3450](#3450)            name.push_str("-");
[3451](#3451)        }
[3452](#3452)        FunctionKind::Freestanding | FunctionKind::AsyncFreestanding => {}
[3453](#3453)    }
[3454](#3454)    name.push_str(func.item_name());
[3455](#3455)    name.to_snake_case()
[3456](#3456)}
[3457](#3457)
[3458](#3458)fn get_resources<'a>(
[3459](#3459)    resolve: &'a Resolve,
[3460](#3460)    id: InterfaceId,
[3461](#3461)) -> impl Iterator<Item = (TypeId, &'a str)> + 'a {
[3462](#3462)    resolve.interfaces[id]
[3463](#3463)        .types
[3464](#3464)        .iter()
[3465](#3465)        .filter_map(move |(name, ty)| match &resolve.types[*ty].kind {
[3466](#3466)            TypeDefKind::Resource => Some((*ty, name.as_str())),
[3467](#3467)            _ => None,
[3468](#3468)        })
[3469](#3469)}
[3470](#3470)
[3471](#3471)fn get_resource_functions<'a>(resolve: &'a Resolve, resource_id: TypeId) -> Vec<&'a Function> {
[3472](#3472)    let resource = &resolve.types[resource_id];
[3473](#3473)    match resource.owner {
[3474](#3474)        TypeOwner::World(id) => resolve.worlds[id]
[3475](#3475)            .imports
[3476](#3476)            .values()
[3477](#3477)            .filter_map(|item| match item {
[3478](#3478)                WorldItem::Function(f) => Some(f),
[3479](#3479)                _ => None,
[3480](#3480)            })
[3481](#3481)            .filter(|f| f.kind.resource() == Some(resource_id))
[3482](#3482)            .collect(),
[3483](#3483)        TypeOwner::Interface(id) => resolve.interfaces[id]
[3484](#3484)            .functions
[3485](#3485)            .values()
[3486](#3486)            .filter(|f| f.kind.resource() == Some(resource_id))
[3487](#3487)            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
[3488](#3488)        TypeOwner::None => {
[3489](#3489)            panic!("A resource must be owned by a world or interface");
[3490](#3490)        }
[3491](#3491)    }
[3492](#3492)}
[3493](#3493)
[3494](#3494)fn get_world_resources<'a>(
[3495](#3495)    resolve: &'a Resolve,
[3496](#3496)    id: WorldId,
[3497](#3497)) -> impl Iterator<Item = (TypeId, &'a str)> + 'a {
[3498](#3498)    resolve.worlds[id]
[3499](#3499)        .imports
[3500](#3500)        .iter()
[3501](#3501)        .filter_map(move |(name, item)| match item {
[3502](#3502)            WorldItem::Type(id) => match resolve.types[*id].kind {
[3503](#3503)                TypeDefKind::Resource => Some(match name {
[3504](#3504)                    WorldKey::Name(s) => (*id, s.as_str()),
[3505](#3505)                    WorldKey::Interface(_) => unreachable!(),
[3506](#3506)                }),
[3507](#3507)                _ => None,
[3508](#3508)            },
[3509](#3509)            _ => None,
[3510](#3510)        })

# AsyncConfig in wasmtime_wit_bindgen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasmtime-wit-bindgen/34.0.2/wasmtime_wit_bindgen/enum.AsyncConfig.html

```
pub enum AsyncConfig {
    None,
    All,
    AllExceptImports(
```
[HashSet](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/collections/hash/set/struct.HashSet.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>),
    OnlyImports([HashSet](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/collections/hash/set/struct.HashSet.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>),
}## Expand description

Which imports should be generated as async functions.

The imports should be declared in the following format:

- Regular functions: `"{function-name}"`
- Resource methods: `"[method]{resource-name}.{method-name}"`
- Resource destructors: `"[drop]{resource-name}"`

Examples:

- Regular function: `"get-environment"`
- Resource method: `"[method]input-stream.read"`
- Resource destructor: `"[drop]input-stream"`

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.None)

### None

No functions are `async`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.All)

### All

All generated functions should be `async`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.AllExceptImports)

These imported functions should not be async, but everything else is.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.OnlyImports)

These functions are the only imports that are async, all other imports are sync.

Note that all exports are still async in this situation.

# wasmtime-wit-bindgen 34.0.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wasmtime-wit-bindgen/latest/builds

All the builds on docs.rs are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The limits for this crate are the following:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                    If a build fails because it hit one of those limits please
                    [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                    to get them increased.

# anyhow 1.0.103 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/anyhow/^1.0.93

# Anyhow ¯\_(°ペ)_/¯

This library provides [ anyhow::Error](https://docs.rs/anyhow/1.0/anyhow/struct.Error.html), a trait object based error type
for easy idiomatic error handling in Rust applications.

```
[]
 = "1.0"
```
## Details

-
Use `Result<T, anyhow::Error>`, or equivalently`anyhow::Result<T>`, as the return type of any fallible function.Within the function, use `?`to easily propagate any error that implements the`std::error::Error``use Result;`
-
Attach context to help the person troubleshooting the error understand where things went wrong. A low-level error like "No such file or directory" can be annoying to debug without more context about what higher level step the application was in the middle of. `use ;``Error: Failed to read instrs from ./path/to/instrs.json Caused by: No such file or directory (os error 2)`
-
Downcasting is supported and can be by value, by shared reference, or by mutable reference as needed. `// If the error was caused by redaction, then return a // tombstone instead of the content. match root_cause.`
-
If using Rust ≥ 1.65, a backtrace is captured and printed with the error if the underlying error type does not already provide its own. In order to see backtraces, they must be enabled through the environment variables described in `std::backtrace`- If you want panics and errors to both have backtraces, set
`RUST_BACKTRACE=1`;
- If you want only errors to have backtraces, set `RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE=1`;
- If you want only panics to have backtraces, set `RUST_BACKTRACE=1`and`RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE=0`.

- If you want panics and errors to both have backtraces, set
-
Anyhow works with any error type that has an impl of `std::error::Error`, including ones defined in your crate. We do not bundle a`derive(Error)`macro but you can write the impls yourself or use a standalone macro like[thiserror](https://github.com/dtolnay/thiserror).`use Error;`
-
One-off error messages can be constructed using the `anyhow!`macro, which supports string interpolation and produces an`anyhow::Error`.`return Err;`A `bail!`macro is provided as a shorthand for the same early return.`bail!;`

## No-std support

In no_std mode, almost all of the same API is available and works the same way. To depend on Anyhow in no_std mode, disable our default enabled "std" feature in Cargo.toml. A global allocator is required.

```
[]
 = {  = "1.0",  = false }
```
With versions of Rust older than 1.81, no_std mode may require an additional
`.map_err(Error::msg)` when working with a non-Anyhow error type inside a
function that returns Anyhow's error type, as the trait that `?`-based error
conversions are defined by is only available in std in those old versions.

## Comparison to failure

The `anyhow::Error` type works something like `failure::Error`, but unlike
failure ours is built around the standard library's `std::error::Error` trait
rather than a separate trait `failure::Fail`. The standard library has adopted
the necessary improvements for this to be possible as part of [RFC 2504](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/blob/master/text/2504-fix-error.md).

## Comparison to thiserror

Use Anyhow if you don't care what error type your functions return, you just
want it to be easy. This is common in application code. Use [thiserror](https://github.com/dtolnay/thiserror) if you
are a library that wants to design your own dedicated error type(s) so that on
failures the caller gets exactly the information that you choose.

---

# heck 0.5.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/heck/^0.5

**heck** is a case conversion library

This library exists to provide case conversion between common cases like CamelCase and snake_case. It is intended to be unicode aware, internally consistent, and reasonably well performing.

## Definition of a word boundary

Word boundaries are defined by non-alphanumeric characters, as well as within those words in this manner:

- If an uppercase character is followed by lowercase letters, a word boundary is considered to be just prior to that uppercase character.
- If multiple uppercase characters are consecutive, they are considered to be within a single word, except that the last will be part of the next word if it is followed by lowercase characters (see rule 1).

That is, "HelloWorld" is segmented `Hello|World` whereas "XMLHttpRequest" is
segmented `XML|Http|Request`.

Characters not within words (such as spaces, punctuations, and underscores) are not included in the output string except as they are a part of the case being converted to. Multiple adjacent word boundaries (such as a series of underscores) are folded into one. ("hello__world" in snake case is therefore "hello_world", not the exact same string). Leading or trailing word boundary indicators are dropped, except insofar as CamelCase capitalizes the first word.

## Cases contained in this library:

- UpperCamelCase
- lowerCamelCase
- snake_case
- kebab-case
- SHOUTY_SNAKE_CASE
- Title Case
- SHOUTY-KEBAB-CASE
- Train-Case

## MSRV

The minimum supported Rust version for this crate is 1.56.0. This may change in minor or patch releases, but we probably won't ever require a very recent version. If you would like to have a stronger guarantee than that, please open an issue.

## License

heck is distributed under the terms of both the MIT license and the Apache License (Version 2.0).

See LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT for details.

# indexmap 2.14.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/indexmap/^2.0.0

# indexmap

A pure-Rust hash table which preserves (in a limited sense) insertion order.

This crate implements compact map and set data-structures, where the iteration order of the keys is independent from their hash or value. It preserves insertion order (except after removals), and it allows lookup of entries by either hash table key or numerical index.

Note: this crate was originally released under the name `ordermap`,
but it was renamed to `indexmap` to better reflect its features.
The [ ordermap](https://crates.io/crates/ordermap) crate now exists
as a wrapper over

`indexmap` with stronger ordering properties.# Background

This was inspired by Python 3.6's new dict implementation (which remembers the insertion order and is fast to iterate, and is compact in memory).

Some of those features were translated to Rust, and some were not. The result was indexmap, a hash table that has following properties:

- Order is **independent of hash function**and hash values of keys.
- Fast to iterate.
- Indexed in compact space.
- Preserves insertion order **as long**as you don't call`.remove()`,`.swap_remove()`, or other methods that explicitly change order. The alternate`.shift_remove()`does preserve relative order.
- Uses hashbrown for the inner table, just like Rust's libstd `HashMap`does.

## Performance

`IndexMap` derives a couple of performance facts directly from how it is constructed,
which is roughly:

A raw hash table of key-value indices, and a vector of key-value pairs.

-
Iteration is very fast since it is on the dense key-values.
-
Removal is fast since it moves memory areas only in the table, and uses a single swap in the vector.
-
Lookup is fast-ish because the initial 7-bit hash lookup uses SIMD, and indices are densely stored. Lookup also is slow-ish since the actual key-value pairs are stored separately. (Visible when cpu caches size is limiting.)
-
In practice, `IndexMap`has been tested out as the hashmap in rustc in[PR45282](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/45282)and the performance was roughly on par across the whole workload.
-
If you want the properties of `IndexMap`, or its strongest performance points fits your workload, it might be the best hash table implementation.

# Recent Changes

See [RELEASES.md](https://github.com/indexmap-rs/indexmap/blob/main/RELEASES.md).

---

# wit-parser 0.233.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wit-parser/^0.233.0

`wit-parser`

A Rust crate for parsing and interpreting the [ *.wit](https://github.com/WebAssembly/component-model/blob/main/design/mvp/WIT.md) text format. This
text format is used to describe the imports and exports of a

[component](https://github.com/webassembly/component-model).

This crate is a low-level tooling crate which is intended to be integrated
further into toolchains elsewhere and isn't necessarily interacted with on a
day-to-day basis. Internally it supports parsing a `*.wit` document into a
structured AST. Additionally it implements mechanisms of the canonical ABI to
assist in binding the canonical ABI into various languages.

# anyhow 1.0.103 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/anyhow/1.0.103

# Anyhow ¯\_(°ペ)_/¯

This library provides [ anyhow::Error](https://docs.rs/anyhow/1.0/anyhow/struct.Error.html), a trait object based error type
for easy idiomatic error handling in Rust applications.

```
[]
 = "1.0"
```
## Details

-
Use `Result<T, anyhow::Error>`, or equivalently`anyhow::Result<T>`, as the return type of any fallible function.Within the function, use `?`to easily propagate any error that implements the`std::error::Error``use Result;`
-
Attach context to help the person troubleshooting the error understand where things went wrong. A low-level error like "No such file or directory" can be annoying to debug without more context about what higher level step the application was in the middle of. `use ;``Error: Failed to read instrs from ./path/to/instrs.json Caused by: No such file or directory (os error 2)`
-
Downcasting is supported and can be by value, by shared reference, or by mutable reference as needed. `// If the error was caused by redaction, then return a // tombstone instead of the content. match root_cause.`
-
If using Rust ≥ 1.65, a backtrace is captured and printed with the error if the underlying error type does not already provide its own. In order to see backtraces, they must be enabled through the environment variables described in `std::backtrace`- If you want panics and errors to both have backtraces, set
`RUST_BACKTRACE=1`;
- If you want only errors to have backtraces, set `RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE=1`;
- If you want only panics to have backtraces, set `RUST_BACKTRACE=1`and`RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE=0`.

- If you want panics and errors to both have backtraces, set
-
Anyhow works with any error type that has an impl of `std::error::Error`, including ones defined in your crate. We do not bundle a`derive(Error)`macro but you can write the impls yourself or use a standalone macro like[thiserror](https://github.com/dtolnay/thiserror).`use Error;`
-
One-off error messages can be constructed using the `anyhow!`macro, which supports string interpolation and produces an`anyhow::Error`.`return Err;`A `bail!`macro is provided as a shorthand for the same early return.`bail!;`

## No-std support

In no_std mode, almost all of the same API is available and works the same way. To depend on Anyhow in no_std mode, disable our default enabled "std" feature in Cargo.toml. A global allocator is required.

```
[]
 = {  = "1.0",  = false }
```
With versions of Rust older than 1.81, no_std mode may require an additional
`.map_err(Error::msg)` when working with a non-Anyhow error type inside a
function that returns Anyhow's error type, as the trait that `?`-based error
conversions are defined by is only available in std in those old versions.

## Comparison to failure

The `anyhow::Error` type works something like `failure::Error`, but unlike
failure ours is built around the standard library's `std::error::Error` trait
rather than a separate trait `failure::Fail`. The standard library has adopted
the necessary improvements for this to be possible as part of [RFC 2504](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/blob/master/text/2504-fix-error.md).

## Comparison to thiserror

Use Anyhow if you don't care what error type your functions return, you just
want it to be easy. This is common in application code. Use [thiserror](https://github.com/dtolnay/thiserror) if you
are a library that wants to design your own dedicated error type(s) so that on
failures the caller gets exactly the information that you choose.

---

# futures - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/futures/^0.3/

## Expand description

Abstractions for asynchronous programming.

This crate provides a number of core abstractions for writing asynchronous code:

- [Futures](https://docs.rs/future/index.html)are single eventual values produced by asynchronous computations. Some programming languages (e.g. JavaScript) call this concept “promise”.
- [Streams](https://docs.rs/stream/index.html)represent a series of values produced asynchronously.
- [Sinks](https://docs.rs/sink/index.html)provide support for asynchronous writing of data.
- [Executors](https://docs.rs/executor/index.html)are responsible for running asynchronous tasks.

The crate also contains abstractions for [asynchronous I/O](https://docs.rs/io/index.html) and
[cross-task communication](https://docs.rs/channel/index.html).

Underlying all of this is the *task system*, which is a form of lightweight
threading. Large asynchronous computations are built up using futures,
streams and sinks, and then spawned as independent tasks that are run to
completion, but *do not block* the thread running them.

The following example describes how the task system context is built and used within macros and keywords such as async and await!.

```
fn main() {
    let pool = ThreadPool::new().expect("Failed to build pool");
    let (tx, rx) = mpsc::unbounded::<i32>();
    // Create a future by an async block, where async is responsible for an
    // implementation of Future. At this point no executor has been provided
    // to this future, so it will not be running.
    let fut_values = async {
        // Create another async block, again where the Future implementation
        // is generated by async. Since this is inside of a parent async block,
        // it will be provided with the executor of the parent block when the parent
        // block is executed.
        //
        // This executor chaining is done by Future::poll whose second argument
        // is a std::task::Context. This represents our executor, and the Future
        // implemented by this async block can be polled using the parent async
        // block's executor.
        let fut_tx_result = async move {
            (0..100).for_each(|v| {
                tx.unbounded_send(v).expect("Failed to send");
            })
        };
        // Use the provided thread pool to spawn the generated future
        // responsible for transmission
        pool.spawn_ok(fut_tx_result);
        let fut_values = rx
            .map(|v| v * 2)
            .collect();
        // Use the executor provided to this async block to wait for the
        // future to complete.
        fut_values.await
    };
    // Actually execute the above future, which will invoke Future::poll and
    // subsequently chain appropriate Future::poll and methods needing executors
    // to drive all futures. Eventually fut_values will be driven to completion.
    let values: Vec<i32> = executor::block_on(fut_values);
    println!("Values={:?}", values);
}
```
The majority of examples and code snippets in this crate assume that they are inside an async block as written above.

- `pub use futures_util::stream::`- [TryStreamExt](https://docs.rs/stream/trait.TryStreamExt.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [channel](https://docs.rs/channel/index.html)- `alloc`
- Asynchronous channels.
- [compat](https://docs.rs/compat/index.html)- `compat`
- Interop between `futures`0.1 and 0.3.
- [executor](https://docs.rs/executor/index.html)- `executor`
- Built-in executors and related tools.
- [future](https://docs.rs/future/index.html)
- Asynchronous values.
- [io](https://docs.rs/io/index.html)- `io`and- `std`
- Asynchronous I/O.
- [lock](https://docs.rs/lock/index.html)- `alloc`
- Futures-powered synchronization primitives.
- [never](https://docs.rs/never/index.html)
- This module contains the `Never`type.
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- A “prelude” for crates using the `futures`crate.
- [sink](https://docs.rs/sink/index.html)- `sink`
- Asynchronous sinks.
- [stream](https://docs.rs/stream/index.html)
- Asynchronous streams.
- [task](https://docs.rs/task/index.html)
- Tools for working with tasks.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [join](https://docs.rs/macro.join.html)- `async-await`
- Polls multiple futures simultaneously, returning a tuple of all results once complete.
- [pending](https://docs.rs/macro.pending.html)- `async-await`
- A macro which yields to the event loop once.
- [pin_mut](https://docs.rs/macro.pin_mut.html)
- Pins a value on the stack.
- [poll](https://docs.rs/macro.poll.html)- `async-await`
- A macro which returns the result of polling a future once within the
current `async`context.
- [ready](https://docs.rs/macro.ready.html)
- Extracts the successful type of `Poll<T>`.
- [select](https://docs.rs/macro.select.html)- `async-await`and- `std`
- Polls multiple futures and streams simultaneously, executing the branch
for the future that finishes first. If multiple futures are ready,
one will be pseudo-randomly selected at runtime. Futures directly
passed to `select!`must be`Unpin`and implement`FusedFuture`.
- [select_](https://docs.rs/macro.select_biased.html)- biased - `async-await`
- Polls multiple futures and streams simultaneously, executing the branch
for the future that finishes first. Unlike `select!``select_biased!`must be`Unpin`and implement`FusedFuture`.
- [stream_](https://docs.rs/macro.stream_select.html)- select - `async-await`and- `std`
- Combines several streams, all producing the same `Item`type, into one stream. This is similar to`select_all`but does not require the streams to all be the same type. It also keeps the streams inline, and does not require`Box<dyn Stream>`s to be allocated. Streams passed to this macro must be`Unpin`.
- [try_](https://docs.rs/macro.try_join.html)- join - `async-await`
- Polls multiple futures simultaneously, resolving to a `Result`

# rustversion - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustversion/^1.0.6/

## Expand description

This crate provides macros for conditional compilation according to rustc
compiler version, analogous to [ #[cfg(...)]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/conditional-compilation.html#the-cfg-attribute) and

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/conditional-compilation.html#the-cfg_attr-attribute)

`#[cfg_attr(...)]`[§](https://docs.rs#selectors)Selectors

- `#[rustversion::stable]`
 True on any stable compiler.
- `#[rustversion::stable(1.34)]`
 True on exactly the specified stable compiler.
- `#[rustversion::beta]`
 True on any beta compiler.
- `#[rustversion::nightly]`
 True on any nightly compiler or dev build.
- `#[rustversion::nightly(2025-01-01)]`
 True on exactly one nightly.
- `#[rustversion::since(1.34)]`
 True on that stable release and any later compiler, including beta and nightly.
- `#[rustversion::since(2025-01-01)]`
 True on that nightly and all newer ones.
- `#[rustversion::before(`- *version or date*- `)]`
 Negative of- *#[rustversion::since(...)]*.
- `#[rustversion::not(`- *selector*- `)]`
 Negative of any selector; for example- *#[rustversion::not(nightly)]*.
- `#[rustversion::any(`- *selectors...*- `)]`
 True if any of the comma-separated selectors is true; for example- *#[rustversion::any(stable, beta)]*.
- `#[rustversion::all(`- *selectors...*- `)]`
 True if all of the comma-separated selectors are true; for example- *#[rustversion::all(since(1.31), before(1.34))]*.
- `#[rustversion::attr(`- *selector*- `,`- *attribute*- `)]`
 For conditional inclusion of attributes; analogous to- `cfg_attr`.
- `rustversion::cfg!(`- *selector*- `)`
 An expression form of any of the above attributes; for example- *if rustversion::cfg!(any(stable, beta)) { ... }*.

[§](https://docs.rs#use-cases)Use cases

Providing additional trait impls as types are stabilized in the standard library
without breaking compatibility with older compilers; in this case Pin<P>
stabilized in [Rust 1.33](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2019/02/28/Rust-1.33.0.html#pinning):

```
#[rustversion::since(1.33)]
use std::pin::Pin;
#[rustversion::since(1.33)]
impl<P: MyTrait> MyTrait for Pin<P> {
    /* ... */
}
```
Similar but for language features; the ability to control alignment greater than
1 of packed structs was stabilized in [Rust 1.33](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/master/RELEASES.md#version-1330-2019-02-28).

```
#[rustversion::attr(before(1.33), repr(packed))]
#[rustversion::attr(since(1.33), repr(packed(2)))]
struct Six(i16, i32);
fn main() {
    println!("{}", std::mem::align_of::<Six>());
}
```
Augmenting code with `const` as const impls are stabilized in the standard
library. This use of `const` as an attribute is recognized as a special case
by the rustversion::attr macro.

```
use std::time::Duration;
#[rustversion::attr(since(1.32), const)]
fn duration_as_days(dur: Duration) -> u64 {
    dur.as_secs() / 60 / 60 / 24
}
```
Emitting Cargo cfg directives from a build script. Note that this requires
listing `rustversion` under `[build-dependencies]` in Cargo.toml, not
`[dependencies]`.

```
// build.rs
fn main() {
    if rustversion::cfg!(since(1.36)) {
        println!("cargo:rustc-cfg=no_std");
    }
}
```
```
// src/lib.rs
#![cfg_attr(no_std, no_std)]
#[cfg(no_std)]
extern crate alloc;
```

---

# syn - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/syn/^2.0/

## Expand description

Syn is a parsing library for parsing a stream of Rust tokens into a syntax tree of Rust source code.

Currently this library is geared toward use in Rust procedural macros, but contains some APIs that may be useful more generally.

-
**Data structures**— Syn provides a complete syntax tree that can represent any valid Rust source code. The syntax tree is rooted at`syn::File``syn::Item``syn::Expr``syn::Type`
-
**Derives**— Of particular interest to derive macros is`syn::DeriveInput`
-
**Parsing**— Parsing in Syn is built around[parser functions](https://docs.rs/parse/index.html)with the signature`fn(ParseStream) -> Result<T>`. Every syntax tree node defined by Syn is individually parsable and may be used as a building block for custom syntaxes, or you may dream up your own brand new syntax without involving any of our syntax tree types.
-
**Location information**— Every token parsed by Syn is associated with a`Span`that tracks line and column information back to the source of that token. These spans allow a procedural macro to display detailed error messages pointing to all the right places in the user’s code. There is an example of this below.
-
**Feature flags**— Functionality is aggressively feature gated so your procedural macros enable only what they need, and do not pay in compile time for all the rest.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-of-a-derive-macro)Example of a derive macro

The canonical derive macro using Syn looks like this. We write an ordinary
Rust function tagged with a `proc_macro_derive` attribute and the name of
the trait we are deriving. Any time that derive appears in the user’s code,
the Rust compiler passes their data structure as tokens into our macro. We
get to execute arbitrary Rust code to figure out what to do with those
tokens, then hand some tokens back to the compiler to compile into the
user’s crate.

```
[dependencies]
syn = "2.0"
quote = "1.0"
[lib]
proc-macro = true
```
```
use proc_macro::TokenStream;
use quote::quote;
use syn::{parse_macro_input, DeriveInput};
#[proc_macro_derive(MyMacro)]
pub fn my_macro(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
    // Parse the input tokens into a syntax tree
    let input = parse_macro_input!(input as DeriveInput);
    // Build the output, possibly using quasi-quotation
    let expanded = quote! {
        // ...
    };
    // Hand the output tokens back to the compiler
    TokenStream::from(expanded)
}
```
The [ heapsize](https://github.com/dtolnay/syn/tree/master/examples/heapsize) example directory shows a complete working implementation
of a derive macro. The example derives a

`HeapSize` trait which computes an
estimate of the amount of heap memory owned by a value.```
pub trait HeapSize {
    /// Total number of bytes of heap memory owned by `self`.
    fn heap_size_of_children(&self) -> usize;
}
```
The derive macro allows users to write `#[derive(HeapSize)]` on data
structures in their program.

```
#[derive(HeapSize)]
struct Demo<'a, T: ?Sized> {
    a: Box<T>,
    b: u8,
    c: &'a str,
    d: String,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#spans-and-error-reporting)Spans and error reporting

The token-based procedural macro API provides great control over where the
compiler’s error messages are displayed in user code. Consider the error the
user sees if one of their field types does not implement `HeapSize`.

```
#[derive(HeapSize)]
struct Broken {
    ok: String,
    bad: std::thread::Thread,
}
```
By tracking span information all the way through the expansion of a
procedural macro as shown in the `heapsize` example, token-based macros in
Syn are able to trigger errors that directly pinpoint the source of the
problem.

```
error[E0277]: the trait bound `std::thread::Thread: HeapSize` is not satisfied
 --> src/main.rs:7:5
  |
7 |     bad: std::thread::Thread,
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ the trait `HeapSize` is not implemented for `Thread`
```
[§](https://docs.rs#parsing-a-custom-syntax)Parsing a custom syntax

The [ lazy-static](https://github.com/dtolnay/syn/tree/master/examples/lazy-static) example directory shows the implementation of a

`functionlike!(...)` procedural macro in which the input tokens are parsed
using Syn’s parsing API.The example reimplements the popular `lazy_static` crate from crates.io as a
procedural macro.

```
lazy_static! {
    static ref USERNAME: Regex = Regex::new("^[a-z0-9_-]{3,16}$").unwrap();
}
```
The implementation shows how to trigger custom warnings and error messages on the macro input.

```
warning: come on, pick a more creative name
  --> src/main.rs:10:16
   |
10 |     static ref FOO: String = "lazy_static".to_owned();
   |                ^^^
```
[§](https://docs.rs#testing)Testing

When testing macros, we often care not just that the macro can be used
successfully but also that when the macro is provided with invalid input it
produces maximally helpful error messages. Consider using the [ trybuild](https://github.com/dtolnay/trybuild)
crate to write tests for errors that are emitted by your macro or errors
detected by the Rust compiler in the expanded code following misuse of the
macro. Such tests help avoid regressions from later refactors that
mistakenly make an error no longer trigger or be less helpful than it used
to be.

[§](https://docs.rs#debugging)Debugging

When developing a procedural macro it can be helpful to look at what the
generated code looks like. Use `cargo rustc -- -Zunstable-options -Zunpretty=expanded` or the [ cargo expand](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-expand) subcommand.

To show the expanded code for some crate that uses your procedural macro,
run `cargo expand` from that crate. To show the expanded code for one of
your own test cases, run `cargo expand --test the_test_case` where the last
argument is the name of the test file without the `.rs` extension.

This write-up by Brandon W Maister discusses debugging in more detail:
[Debugging Rust’s new Custom Derive system](https://quodlibetor.github.io/posts/debugging-rusts-new-custom-derive-system/).

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-features)Optional features

Syn puts a lot of functionality behind optional features in order to optimize compile time for the most common use cases. The following features are available.

- `derive`- *(enabled by default)*— Data structures for representing the possible input to a derive macro, including structs and enums and types.
- `full`
- `parsing`- *(enabled by default)*— Ability to parse input tokens into a syntax tree node of a chosen type.
- `printing`- *(enabled by default)*— Ability to print a syntax tree node as tokens of Rust source code.
- `visit`
- `visit-mut`
- `fold`
- `clone-impls`- *(enabled by default)*— Clone impls for all syntax tree types.
- `extra-traits`
- `proc-macro`- *(enabled by default)*— Runtime dependency on the dynamic library libproc_macro from rustc toolchain.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [buffer](https://docs.rs/buffer/index.html)- `parsing`
- A stably addressed token buffer supporting efficient traversal based on a cheaply copyable cursor.
- [ext](https://docs.rs/ext/index.html)
- Extension traits to provide parsing methods on foreign types.
- [fold](https://docs.rs/fold/index.html)- `fold`
- Syntax tree traversal to transform the nodes of an owned syntax tree.
- [meta](https://docs.rs/meta/index.html)- `parsing`and (- `derive`or- `full`)
- Facility for interpreting structured content inside of an `Attribute`.
- [parse](https://docs.rs/parse/index.html)- `parsing`
- Parsing interface for parsing a token stream into a syntax tree node.
- [punctuated](https://docs.rs/punctuated/index.html)
- A punctuated sequence of syntax tree nodes separated by punctuation.
- [spanned](https://docs.rs/spanned/index.html)- `parsing`and- `printing`
- A trait that can provide the `Span`of the complete contents of a syntax tree node.
- [token](https://docs.rs/token/index.html)
- Tokens representing Rust punctuation, keywords, and delimiters.
- [visit](https://docs.rs/visit/index.html)- `visit`
- Syntax tree traversal to walk a shared borrow of a syntax tree.
- [visit_](https://docs.rs/visit_mut/index.html)- mut - `visit-mut`
- Syntax tree traversal to mutate an exclusive borrow of a syntax tree in place.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [Token](https://docs.rs/macro.Token.html)
- A type-macro that expands to the name of the Rust type representation of a given token.
- [braced](https://docs.rs/macro.braced.html)- `parsing`
- Parse a set of curly braces and expose their content to subsequent parsers.
- [bracketed](https://docs.rs/macro.bracketed.html)- `parsing`
- Parse a set of square brackets and expose their content to subsequent parsers.
- [custom_](https://docs.rs/macro.custom_keyword.html)- keyword
- Define a type that supports parsing and printing a given identifier as if it were a keyword.
- [custom_](https://docs.rs/macro.custom_punctuation.html)- punctuation
- Define a type that supports parsing and printing a multi-character symbol as if it were a punctuation token.
- [parenthesized](https://docs.rs/macro.parenthesized.html)- `parsing`
- Parse a set of parentheses and expose their content to subsequent parsers.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/macro.parse_macro_input.html)- macro_ - input - `parsing`and- `proc-macro`
- Parse the input TokenStream of a macro, triggering a compile error if the tokens fail to parse.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/macro.parse_quote.html)- quote - `parsing`and- `printing`
- Quasi-quotation macro that accepts input like the `quote!`
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/macro.parse_quote_spanned.html)- quote_ - spanned - `parsing`and- `printing`
- This macro is `parse_quote!``quote_spanned!`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Abi](https://docs.rs/struct.Abi.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- The binary interface of a function: `extern "C"`.
- [Angle](https://docs.rs/struct.AngleBracketedGenericArguments.html)- Bracketed - Generic - Arguments - `derive`or- `full`

- [Attribute](https://docs.rs/struct.Attribute.html)- `derive`or- `full`

- [Bare](https://docs.rs/struct.BareFnArg.html)- FnArg - `derive`or- `full`

- An await expression: `fut.await`.

- A binary operation: `a + b`,`a += b`.

- A lifetime labeling a `for`,`while`, or`loop`.
- [Lifetime](https://docs.rs/struct.Lifetime.html)
- A Rust lifetime: `'a`.
- [Lifetime](https://docs.rs/struct.LifetimeParam.html)- Param - `derive`or- `full`

- [LitBool](https://docs.rs/struct.LitBool.html)

- [LitByte](https://docs.rs/struct.LitByte.html)

- [LitByte](https://docs.rs/struct.LitByteStr.html)- Str

- [LitCStr](https://docs.rs/struct.LitCStr.html)

- [LitChar](https://docs.rs/struct.LitChar.html)
- A character literal: `'a'`.

- [LitInt](https://docs.rs/struct.LitInt.html)

- [LitStr](https://docs.rs/struct.LitStr.html)
- A UTF-8 string literal: `"foo"`.

- [Local](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalInit.html)- Init - `full`

- Arguments of a function path segment: the `(A, B) -> C`in`Fn(A,B) -> C`.
- [PatConst](https://docs.rs/struct.PatConst.html)- `full`

- [PatIdent](https://docs.rs/struct.PatIdent.html)- `full`
- A pattern that binds a new variable: `ref mut binding @ SUBPATTERN`.
- [PatLit](https://docs.rs/struct.PatLit.html)- `full`
